gita-2-11.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is grieving for people he does not need to grieve for, even though he talks like a wise man. Wise people do not grieve for the living or for the dead.

gita-2-12.plain: Krishna says that he, Arjuna and all these kings have always existed. None of them will ever stop existing in the future.

gita-2-13.plain: The soul living in the body goes through childhood, youth and old age. In the same way, at death it moves on to a new body, and a calm person is not upset by this.

gita-2-14.plain: Krishna calls Arjuna "son of Kunti" (Kunti is Arjuna's mother). He says that when our senses meet the world, we feel cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These feelings come and go and do not last, so Arjuna should bear them bravely.

gita-2-15.plain: A person who is not shaken by pain or pleasure stays steady and calm in both. That person is ready for eternal life.

gita-2-16.plain: Things that are not real do not truly exist, and what is truly real never stops existing. People who see deeply into things have understood the difference.

gita-2-17.plain: Krishna says the soul fills everything and cannot be destroyed. No one can destroy what lasts forever.

gita-2-18.plain: Bodies come to an end, but the soul inside them is eternal, cannot be destroyed, and cannot be measured. So Krishna tells Arjuna to fight.

gita-2-19.plain: Anyone who thinks the soul kills, or thinks the soul gets killed, does not understand. The soul does not kill, and it cannot be killed.

gita-2-20.plain: The soul is never born and never dies. It has always been and will always be, and it is not killed when the body is killed.

gita-2-21.plain: Krishna calls Arjuna "Partha," son of Pritha. He asks how a person who knows the soul is eternal and unborn could truly kill anyone or make anyone be killed.

gita-2-22.plain: A person throws away worn-out clothes and puts on new ones. In the same way, the soul leaves worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

gita-2-23.plain: Weapons cannot cut the soul and fire cannot burn it. Water cannot make it wet and wind cannot dry it.

gita-2-24.plain: The soul cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, present everywhere, steady, unmoving and very ancient.

gita-2-25.plain: The soul cannot be seen, cannot be fully imagined, and never changes. Knowing this, Arjuna should not grieve.

gita-2-26.plain: Krishna says that even if Arjuna thinks the soul is always being born and always dying, he still should not grieve.

gita-2-27.plain: Everyone who is born will surely die, and everyone who dies will surely be born again. So Arjuna should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.

gita-2-28.plain: Beings are unseen before birth, seen during their life, and unseen again after death. So there is no reason to weep.

gita-2-29.plain: Some people see the soul as a wonder, some speak of it as a wonder, and some hear of it as a wonder. But even after hearing about it, no one truly understands it.

gita-2-30.plain: The soul living in every body can never be harmed. So Arjuna should not grieve for any living being.

gita-17-26.plain: Krishna explains that the word "Sat" means what is real and what is good. It is also used to name a good deed. He calls Arjuna "Partha," meaning son of Pritha.

gita-17-27.plain: Krishna says that sticking faithfully to worship, self-discipline and giving is also called "Sat," or good. Any action done for God is called "Sat" too.

gita-17-28.plain: Krishna says that worship, giving, self-discipline or any other act done without faith is called "Asat," which means unreal or worthless. It brings no good in this life or the next.

gita-18-1.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain clearly the difference between renunciation (giving up actions) and relinquishment (letting go of the results of actions). He uses Krishna's titles, Hrishikesha (lord of the senses) and Keshinishudana (slayer of the demon Keshi).
themes: should I quit or keep going

gita-18-2.plain: Krishna says wise people call it renunciation when you stop doing actions driven by selfish desire. They call it relinquishment when you keep acting but let go of wanting the rewards.

gita-18-3.plain: Krishna reports two opinions. Some thinkers say all action should be given up as bad. Others say worship, giving and self-discipline should never be given up.

gita-18-4.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to listen to his own conclusion about relinquishment. He says there are three kinds of it.
themes: learning the right way to let go

gita-18-5.plain: Krishna says worship, giving and self-discipline should not be dropped. They should be done, because they make wise people purer.

gita-18-6.plain: Krishna says even these good acts should be done without clinging to them and without wanting rewards. He calls this his firm and best view.

gita-18-7.plain: Krishna says it is wrong to give up the duties you are meant to do. Dropping them out of confusion is the lowest, darkest kind of giving up.

gita-18-8.plain: Krishna says if you drop a duty because it is hard or might hurt, that kind of giving up comes from restless desire. It brings none of the real benefit of letting go.

gita-18-9.plain: Krishna says when you do your duty simply because it should be done, without clinging and without wanting rewards, that is the pure kind of letting go.

gita-18-10.plain: Krishna says a truly pure and wise person, free of doubts, does not hate unpleasant work. Nor does that person cling to pleasant work.

gita-18-11.plain: Krishna says no one living in a body can stop acting completely. The real relinquisher is the one who lets go of the results of action.

gita-18-12.plain: Krishna says people who cling to results get good, bad or mixed results after death. People who truly let go get no such results that bind them.

gita-18-13.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to learn from him the five causes behind every action. These come from Sankhya, an ancient school of thought.

gita-18-14.plain: Krishna names the five causes of action. They are the body, the doer, the senses and organs, the different energies, and the guiding divine powers.

gita-18-15.plain: Krishna says every action a person does with body, speech or mind, right or wrong, comes from these five causes together.
themes: why we do what we do

gita-18-16.plain: Krishna says since action comes from these five causes, a person with untrained thinking who believes the true Self is the doer has a twisted view. That person does not see clearly.

gita-18-17.plain: Krishna says a person with no selfish sense of "I am the doer," whose mind is not stained, does not really kill even when killing in battle. That person is not bound by the action.

gita-1-41.plain: Arjuna continues his argument to Krishna, here called Vārshneya, meaning "descendant of the Vrishni clan." He says that when a family loses its rules, its women go astray, and the social order of castes (inherited social classes) gets mixed up.

gita-1-42.plain: Arjuna says this mixing of the social order sends both the family and those who destroyed it to hell. He adds that the ancestors suffer too, because no one is left to offer them the rice-balls and water of the traditional memorial rites.

gita-1-43.plain: Arjuna says that the wrongdoing of those who destroy a family wipes out the old customs of both caste and family.

gita-1-44.plain: Arjuna tells Krishna, here called Janārdana, that people whose family customs are lost live in hell forever. He says this is what he has been taught.
themes: relying on what we were taught

gita-1-45.plain: Arjuna cries out that they are about to commit a great sin. He says they are ready to kill their own relatives just because they want the pleasures of being king.

gita-1-46.plain: Arjuna says it would be better if the sons of Dhritarāshtra, the blind king, killed him while he stood unarmed and did not fight back.

gita-1-47.plain: Sanjaya, the narrator, says that after speaking, Arjuna sat down in his chariot. Overwhelmed by grief, he threw away his bow and arrows.

gita-2-1.plain: Sanjaya describes Arjuna full of pity, with tears in his eyes and lost in sadness. Then Krishna, called Madhusūdana ("slayer of the demon Madhu"), begins to speak to him.

gita-2-2.plain: Krishna asks Arjuna where this weakness has come from at such a dangerous moment. He says it is unworthy of a noble person, brings shame, and keeps one from heaven.
themes: losing nerve at a crucial moment

gita-2-3.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, whom he calls Pārtha ("son of Prithā") and Parantapa ("burner of foes"), not to give in to weakness because it does not suit him. He tells him to shake off this small-hearted fear and stand up.
themes: motivation when you want to quit

gita-2-4.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna how he can shoot arrows at Bhīshma, his great-uncle, and Drona, his teacher. These are men he should honor and respect.

gita-2-5.plain: Arjuna says it would be better to live as a beggar than to kill his noble teachers, who wish him well. Any riches he won by killing them would feel stained with their blood.
themes: guilt over success at others' cost

gita-2-6.plain: Arjuna says he does not know which is worse, winning or losing. If they killed their cousins, the sons of Dhritarāshtra, they would not even want to go on living.

gita-2-7.plain: Arjuna admits that weakness has taken over his heart and that he is confused about his duty. He asks Krishna to tell him clearly what is best, saying he is now Krishna's student and begs to be taught.

gita-2-8.plain: Arjuna says that even ruling the whole earth, or ruling over the gods (the "Shining Ones"), would not take away the deep pain that is drying up his senses.

gita-2-9.plain: Sanjaya says that Arjuna, called Gudākesha ("conqueror of sleep"), told Krishna "I will not fight!" and then fell silent.

gita-2-10.plain: Sanjaya says that Krishna, called Hrishīkesha ("lord of the senses"), almost smiling, spoke to the sad Arjuna there between the two armies.
themes: calm in the middle of chaos

gita-2-31.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that, thinking of his own duty as a Kshattriya (a warrior whose role is to protect), he should not be afraid. For a warrior, nothing is better than a fight for what is right.
themes: standing up for what is right

gita-2-32.plain: Krishna says warriors are lucky when a righteous fight comes to them without their seeking it. Such a fight is like an open door to heaven.
themes: facing challenges that come to you

gita-2-33.plain: Krishna warns that if Arjuna refuses to fight this righteous battle, he will give up his duty and his honor, and that would be a sin.

gita-9-23.plain: Krishna says that people who worship other gods (the "Shining Ones") with real faith are actually worshipping him too. They are just not doing it in the proper, direct way. Arjuna is called "son of Kunti" after his mother.

gita-9-24.plain: Krishna says he is the one who truly receives every offering and rules over all. People who don't understand this about him fall back and miss the highest goal.

gita-9-25.plain: Krishna says people reach whatever they worship. Those who worship gods go to the gods, those who honor their ancestors go to the ancestors, and those who worship nature spirits go to them. Those who worship Krishna come to him.
themes: choosing what to devote your life to

gita-9-26.plain: Krishna says that if someone offers him even a simple leaf, flower, fruit or a little water with love, he gladly accepts it. What matters is the love behind the gift, not its size.
themes: feeling I have nothing to give

gita-9-27.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to make everything he does an offering to God. This includes working, eating, worshipping, giving to others and self-discipline.

gita-9-28.plain: Krishna says that if Arjuna offers all his actions this way, he will be freed from the good and bad results that tie people down. Inwardly steady through letting go, he will become free and come to Krishna.

gita-9-29.plain: Krishna says he treats all beings the same. He hates no one and favors no one. But those who love and worship him live in him, and he lives in them.

gita-9-30.plain: Krishna says that even a person who has done very bad things should be seen as good if he now worships God with his whole heart. This is because he has made the right decision.

gita-9-31.plain: Krishna says such a person quickly becomes good and finds lasting peace. He promises Arjuna ("Kaunteya," son of Kunti) that someone devoted to him is never lost.

gita-9-32.plain: Krishna says anyone who turns to him for shelter can reach the highest goal. This includes people looked down on in his society, such as women, merchants (Vaishyas) and laborers (Shudras). Arjuna is called "Partha," son of Pritha.

gita-9-33.plain: Krishna says that if even these people can reach him, then holy priests (Brahmanas) and saintly kings surely can. Since Arjuna has been born into this short-lived and unhappy world, he should worship Krishna.

gita-9-34.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to keep his mind on him, love him, make offerings to him and bow down to him. If Arjuna does this, with Krishna as his highest goal, he will come to Krishna.

gita-10-1.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to listen again to his highest teaching. He says he is sharing it because Arjuna is dear to him and he wants what is best for him.

gita-10-2.plain: Krishna says even the gods and the great sages (Rishis) do not know where he came from. This is because he is the source of all of them.

gita-10-3.plain: Krishna says that anyone who truly understands him as never born, without beginning, and the great Lord of the world is free from confusion. Such a person is freed from all sin.

gita-10-4.plain: Krishna begins listing qualities found in living beings. They include understanding, wisdom, clear thinking, forgiveness, truth, self-control, calm, pleasure and pain, being and not being, fear and courage.

gita-10-5.plain: Krishna finishes the list: not hurting others, staying balanced, contentment, self-discipline, generosity, fame and disgrace. He says all these different qualities in beings come from him.

gita-10-6.plain: Krishna says the seven great sages, the four ancient ones and the Manus, the first fathers of humankind, were born from his mind. All people come from them.

gita-10-7.plain: Krishna says that whoever truly understands his greatness and power becomes steady in yoga, which means spiritual union with God, that never wavers. There is no doubt about it.

gita-10-8.plain: Krishna says he is the source of everything, and everything grows out of him. Wise people who understand this worship him with deep love and feeling.

gita-4-39.plain: Krishna says that a person who has faith and controls their senses gains true wisdom. Once they have this wisdom, they quickly reach the highest peace.

gita-4-40.plain: Krishna warns that a person who is ignorant, has no faith, and keeps doubting everything ends up ruined. Someone stuck in doubt finds no happiness in this life or the next.

gita-4-41.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Dhananjaya, "winner of wealth") that his actions do not trap a person who works without attachment, who has cut through doubt with wisdom, and who is guided by their true inner self.

gita-4-42.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to use the wisdom of the true self like a sword to cut away the doubt in his heart. That doubt comes from not understanding. Then Arjuna should stay steady in yoga, and stand up and act.

gita-5-1.plain: Arjuna is confused. Krishna has praised giving up action, and he has also praised yoga done through action. Arjuna asks him to say clearly which one is better.

gita-5-2.plain: Krishna answers that both giving up action and doing action as yoga lead to the highest joy. But doing your work in the spirit of yoga is better than giving up work.
themes: should I quit or keep going

gita-5-3.plain: Krishna says that a person who neither hates nor craves things is a true renouncer, even while living an active life. Such a person is not pushed around by opposites like pleasure and pain, so they are easily set free.
themes: staying calm in ups and downs

gita-5-4.plain: Krishna says only beginners think Sankhya (the path of knowledge and giving up action) and Yoga (the path of selfless action) are different. Someone who truly follows either one gets the results of both.

gita-5-5.plain: Krishna says the followers of knowledge and the followers of selfless action reach the same goal. A person who sees that the two paths are really one sees the truth.

gita-5-6.plain: Krishna says that truly giving up action is hard without the practice of yoga. A sage (muni, a quiet thinker) who is steady in yoga quickly reaches the Eternal.

gita-5-7.plain: Krishna says that a person who is steady in yoga, pure, self-controlled, and master of their senses, and who sees their own self in every living being, is not harmed or tied down by their actions, even while acting.

gita-5-8.plain: Krishna says that a wise and steady person thinks, "I am not really the one doing anything." They think this even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping and breathing.

gita-5-9.plain: Krishna continues that while speaking, giving, taking, or even blinking, the wise person understands that it is only the senses dealing with the things they sense, not their true self.

gita-5-10.plain: Krishna says that a person who does their actions as an offering to the Eternal, without clinging to them, is not stained by wrongdoing. They are like a lotus leaf, which stays dry even in the water.
themes: staying pure in a messy world

gita-5-11.plain: Krishna says that yogis give up attachment. They act with their body, mind, thinking and senses only to make themselves purer inside.

gita-5-12.plain: Krishna says that a steady person who lets go of wanting the results of their actions finds lasting peace. A person driven by desire and hooked on results stays trapped.

gita-5-13.plain: Krishna says that the person living in the body lets go of all actions in their mind and rests calmly. The body is like a city with nine gates, meaning its openings like the eyes, ears and mouth. The true self in it neither acts nor makes anything act.

gita-5-14.plain: Krishna says that the Lord of the world does not create people's sense of "I am doing this", or their actions, or the link between actions and their results. All this comes from nature.

gita-5-15.plain: Krishna says that the Lord does not take on anyone's bad deeds or good deeds. People get confused because ignorance covers up their true knowledge.

gita-5-16.plain: Krishna says that when ignorance is destroyed by knowing the true self, wisdom shines like the sun and shows the Supreme.

gita-12-12.plain: Krishna ranks spiritual efforts. Understanding is better than practice done without it, and meditation is better than understanding. Better still is letting go of the results of what you do, and peace comes right after that letting go.

gita-12-13.plain: Krishna begins to describe the kind of person he loves. This person holds no grudge against anyone and is friendly and kind. They are not clingy or self-centered, they stay steady in good times and bad, and they forgive.
themes: staying calm in ups and downs

gita-12-14.plain: Krishna goes on: this person is always content, at peace, self-disciplined and determined. Their mind and understanding are given to God. Such a devotee, a person who loves God, is dear to Krishna.

gita-12-15.plain: Krishna says he loves the person who does not upset others and is not upset by others. This person is free from the restless swings of excitement, anger and fear.

gita-12-16.plain: Krishna says he loves the devotee who does not crave things. This person is pure in heart and skillful, and stays calm and untroubled. They do not act out of selfish ambition.

gita-12-17.plain: Krishna says he loves the devoted person who is not pulled around by strong likes and dislikes, grief or longing. This person has let go of chasing good results and fearing bad ones.

gita-12-18.plain: Krishna continues describing the devotee he loves. This person treats enemies and friends the same way. They stay the same whether people honor them or shame them, and whether life brings cold or heat, pleasure or pain. They do not cling to anything.

gita-12-19.plain: Krishna ends the description: this person takes praise and criticism the same way. They speak little and are happy with whatever comes. They are not tied to one home, they have a steady mind and they are full of devotion. Such a person is dear to Krishna.
themes: being content with what you have

gita-12-20.plain: Krishna says that people who live by these teachings with faith, making him their highest goal, are especially dear to him.

gita-13-1.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna, whom he calls Keshava, to explain matter and spirit. He wants to know what the "Field" is and who the "Knower of the Field" is. He also asks what true wisdom is and what is most worth knowing.

gita-13-2.plain: Krishna explains that the body is called the "Field," and the one inside who is aware of it is called the "Knower of the Field."

gita-13-3.plain: Krishna says he himself is the Knower present in every body. He says that knowing the difference between the body and the one who knows it is real wisdom.

gita-13-4.plain: Krishna says he will now briefly explain what the Field, the body and world, is like, how it changes and where it comes from. He will also explain who the Knower is and what powers he has.
themes: how the body and mind work

gita-13-5.plain: Krishna notes that this truth has been sung by Rishis, ancient wise seers, in many different hymns. It has also been reasoned out in the Brahma-sutras, short sacred verses about the ultimate reality.

gita-13-6.plain: Krishna lists what makes up the Field. It includes the basic elements, the sense of "I," the thinking mind and the hidden source of nature. It also includes the ten senses and organs of action, the mind, and the five kinds of things the senses experience.

gita-13-7.plain: Krishna adds that wanting, disliking, pleasure, pain, the body as a whole, awareness and steadiness are also part of the Field. Feelings and mental states belong to the changing body-mind, not to the true Self.

gita-13-8.plain: Krishna begins listing the qualities that make up true wisdom. They are humility, not showing off, not harming others, forgiveness, honesty, serving one's teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control.

gita-13-9.plain: Krishna continues: wisdom also means not being pulled by sense pleasures and not being self-centered. It means seeing clearly the suffering that comes with birth, death, old age and sickness.

gita-13-10.plain: Krishna adds that wisdom means not clinging, and not tying your whole identity to your children, spouse or home. It means staying calm whether what happens is wanted or unwanted.
themes: staying calm when things go wrong

gita-13-11.plain: Krishna continues: wisdom also includes steady devotion to him with no other goal. It includes liking quiet, solitary places and not craving crowds and social life.

gita-7-21.plain: Krishna says that when people worship any god or divine form with faith, he is the one who makes their faith strong and steady.

gita-7-22.plain: With that faith, the person worships that god and gets what they wish for. But Krishna says he is the one who really grants those gifts.

gita-7-23.plain: Krishna says the rewards people get from worshipping lesser gods for their wishes do not last. Those who worship the gods go to the gods, but those devoted to Krishna come to him.
themes: choosing what to devote my life to

gita-7-24.plain: Krishna says people who do not understand think he is only a visible, limited form. They do not know his highest nature, which is beyond form and never dies.

gita-7-25.plain: Krishna says he is hidden from most people, covered by the magical power that makes the world. Confused people do not know him as the one who was never born and never dies.

gita-7-26.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that he knows every being from the past, present and future, but no one truly knows him.

gita-7-27.plain: Krishna says all beings are confused because they get caught in opposites like pleasure and pain, which come from liking and disliking things. Arjuna is called Bharata (descendant of Bharata) and Parantapa (scorcher of enemies).

gita-7-28.plain: Krishna says people who act rightly and have left their wrongs behind become free from this confusion of opposites. They worship him steadily and keep their promises.

gita-7-29.plain: Krishna says those who take shelter in him and work to be free from the cycle of birth and death come to know the Eternal, the true Self, and the nature of all action.

gita-7-30.plain: Krishna says those who know him as the truth behind the physical world, the gods, and sacred offering keep a steady mind. They know him even at the moment of death.

gita-8-1.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna, whom he calls Purushottama (the highest being), to explain the terms he just used: the Eternal, knowledge of the Self, action, the physical world, and the gods.

gita-8-2.plain: Arjuna, calling Krishna Madhusudana (slayer of the demon Madhu), asks what sacrifice inside the body means, and how self-controlled people know Krishna at the moment of death.

gita-8-3.plain: Krishna answers: the Eternal is the supreme thing that can never be destroyed. Its true nature is the Self. Action is the creative power that brings beings into life.

gita-8-4.plain: Krishna explains that the physical world is his part that changes and passes away. The gods relate to the energy that gives life. Sacrifice refers to Krishna himself living inside each body.

gita-8-5.plain: Krishna says that anyone who thinks of him alone when they die goes to be one with him. There is no doubt about it.

gita-8-6.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, called Kaunteya (son of Kunti), that whatever a person thinks about most when they die is what they become after death.
themes: what we think about shapes us

gita-8-7.plain: So Krishna tells Arjuna to remember him at all times and still do his duty and fight. If his mind and understanding stay fixed on Krishna, he will surely reach him.
themes: keeping God in mind at work

gita-8-8.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, called Partha (son of Pritha), that by steady practice and meditation, with a mind that does not wander, a person reaches the supreme divine Spirit.

gita-8-9.plain: Krishna begins to describe what to meditate on: the ancient, all-knowing ruler of everything, smaller than the smallest, holding up all things, beyond imagining, shining like the sun beyond darkness.

gita-8-10.plain: Krishna continues: at death, the person who stays calm and devoted, and by yoga gathers their life-breath between the eyebrows, reaches this supreme divine Spirit.
themes: meditation at the end of life

gita-11-47.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that he saw this highest, shining, endless form only because Krishna chose to show it to him as a gift. No one before Arjuna has ever seen it.

gita-11-48.plain: Krishna says that no ritual offering, study of the Vedas (the ancient holy books), charity, good deeds or harsh self-denial can earn the sight of this form. Arjuna alone has seen it.
themes: can good deeds earn God's favor

gita-11-49.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna not to be confused or afraid after seeing the terrifying form. He asks him to let go of fear, be glad, and look again at Krishna's familiar shape.

gita-11-50.plain: Sanjaya, the narrator, says that Krishna (called Vasudeva) then took his own gentle form again. The great-souled one comforted the frightened Arjuna.
themes: the story continues after the vision

gita-11-51.plain: Arjuna says that seeing Krishna's gentle human form again has calmed him. He feels like himself again. Janardana is another name for Krishna.

gita-11-52.plain: Krishna says the form Arjuna saw is very hard to see. Even the gods always long to see it.
themes: even the gods long for God
value of what you have been given

gita-11-53.plain: Krishna says that no one can see him the way Arjuna did just by studying the Vedas, doing harsh self-denial, giving charity or making offerings.

gita-11-54.plain: Krishna says that only through loving devotion to him alone can a person truly know him, see him as he really is, and become one with him. Parantapa means 'conqueror of foes,' a name for Arjuna.

gita-11-55.plain: Krishna says that a person comes to him if they do their work for him, treat him as their highest goal, love him, are not clinging to things, and hate no living being.
themes: how to live as a devotee

gita-12-1.plain: Arjuna asks which is better at yoga, meaning the spiritual path: people who lovingly worship Krishna in a personal form, or people who worship the formless, unchanging, unseen reality.
themes: which way of worship is best

gita-12-2.plain: Krishna says the best in yoga are those who keep their minds on him and always worship him with deep faith.
themes: which way of worship is best

gita-12-3.plain: Krishna begins describing people who worship the formless reality. It cannot be destroyed, described or imagined. It is everywhere, never changes and lasts forever.

gita-12-4.plain: Krishna says these people, who control their senses, treat everyone equally and are happy when all beings do well, also reach him.

gita-12-5.plain: Krishna says that the path of the formless is harder. It is difficult for people living in a body to set their hearts on something that has no form.
themes: hard to connect with an abstract God

gita-12-6.plain: Krishna speaks of those who offer all their actions to him, focus on him, and worship him in meditation with their whole heart. The next verse finishes the thought.

gita-12-7.plain: Krishna says he quickly rescues such people from the endless cycle of death and rebirth, because their minds are fixed on him. Partha is a name for Arjuna.
themes: God rescues those who love Him

gita-12-8.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to put his mind and his understanding fully on him. Then he will surely live in Krishna afterward.

gita-12-9.plain: Krishna says that if Arjuna cannot keep his mind steady on him, he should reach him through regular practice. Dhananjaya is a name for Arjuna.

gita-12-10.plain: Krishna says that if even regular practice is too hard, Arjuna should focus on serving him and do his work for Krishna's sake. That way he will still reach perfection.
themes: doing work for a higher purpose
there is a path for everyone

gita-12-11.plain: Krishna says that if even that is too hard, Arjuna should trust in Krishna, control himself, and let go of wanting the results of his actions.
themes: feeling too weak for spiritual life

gita-2-54.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna (here called Keshava) to describe a person whose mind is calm and steady. How does such a person speak, sit and walk?
themes: what does a calm person look like

gita-2-55.plain: Krishna, called by Arjuna's family name Pārtha, is spoken to here, and Krishna answers. A person has a steady mind when they let go of all their cravings and feel content within themselves, without needing things from outside.

gita-2-56.plain: A wise person with a steady mind is not shaken when bad things happen and does not chase after pleasures. They are free from strong craving, fear and anger.

gita-2-57.plain: A person is truly balanced when they are not clingy about anything. Whether good or bad things happen, they do not get carried away by liking or disliking.

gita-2-58.plain: A tortoise can pull its head and legs into its shell. In the same way, a wise person can pull their attention back from the things that tempt the senses. Then their mind is steady.

gita-2-59.plain: A person who stays away from pleasures may stop having them, but the craving for them can still stay inside. Even that craving goes away once the person experiences the Supreme, the highest truth.

gita-2-60.plain: Krishna warns Arjuna, called son of Kuntī after his mother, that the senses are powerful. Even a wise person who is trying hard can have their mind dragged away by them.

gita-2-61.plain: So a person should control all their senses and sit with a calm mind, keeping Krishna as their highest goal. When someone is master of their senses, their mind stays steady.

gita-2-62.plain: When a person keeps thinking about things they enjoy, they start to get attached to them. Attachment turns into wanting, and when the wanting is blocked, anger comes.

gita-2-63.plain: Anger leads to confused thinking. Confused thinking makes a person forget what they have learned, then they lose good judgment, and losing good judgment ruins them.

gita-2-64.plain: A disciplined person can live among all the things of the world without being pulled toward them or pushed away by them. Because they are in control of themselves, they find peace.
themes: not being controlled by likes and dislikes

gita-2-65.plain: When a person finds that peace, all their suffering comes to an end. A peaceful heart soon leads to a calm and steady mind.

gita-2-66.plain: A person who is not self-controlled cannot think clearly or focus. Without focus there is no peace, and without peace there can be no real happiness.

gita-2-67.plain: If the mind follows the wandering senses, it drags away a person's good sense. It is like strong wind pushing a ship off course on the sea.

gita-2-68.plain: So, Arjuna, the person who has fully held back their senses from chasing pleasures has a steady and clear mind.

gita-2-69.plain: What ordinary people ignore, as if asleep, is what the wise person stays awake to. And the things ordinary people are wide awake for seem like darkness to the wise person who truly sees.
themes: feeling out of step with others

gita-2-70.plain: The ocean stays calm and full even though rivers keep flowing into it. In the same way, a person finds peace when desires come to them but do not disturb them. Someone who keeps chasing desires does not find peace.

gita-2-71.plain: A person who gives up all cravings and lives without greed, without thinking 'this is mine', and without pride finds peace.

gita-2-72.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that this is the eternal, divine state. Someone who reaches it is never confused again. If a person is settled in it even at the moment of death, they reach Nirvāna, final union with the Eternal.

gita-3-1.plain: Arjuna is confused. He asks Krishna, calling him Janārdana and Keshava, why Krishna is pushing him into this terrible battle if knowledge is better than action.

gita-13-12.plain: Krishna finishes his list of what true wisdom is. It means staying steady in knowing your true Self and understanding what real knowledge points to. Anything opposed to this is ignorance.

gita-13-13.plain: Krishna says he will now explain the one thing most worth knowing. Knowing it frees a person from death. It is the supreme Eternal, called Brahman, which has no beginning. It cannot be described as simply existing or simply not existing.

gita-13-14.plain: Krishna describes this Eternal as present everywhere. It acts through every hand and foot, sees through every eye and hears everything. It surrounds and fills the whole world.

gita-13-15.plain: The Eternal shines through all the senses, yet it has no senses of its own. It holds up everything without clinging to anything. It is beyond the three qualities of nature, yet it experiences them.

gita-13-16.plain: The Eternal is both outside and inside every living being. It is both still and moving. It is so subtle that we cannot perceive it, and it is both very near and very far away.

gita-13-17.plain: The Eternal is one and undivided, yet it seems split up among all beings. It supports all creatures. It brings them into being, keeps them alive and takes them back at the end.
themes: why things are born and die

gita-13-18.plain: The Eternal is the light behind every light and lies beyond all darkness. It is knowledge itself, the thing to be known, and what knowledge leads to. It lives in the heart of everyone.

gita-13-19.plain: Krishna says he has now briefly explained the Field (the body and the material world), true knowledge and the thing to be known. A devotee who understands this becomes one with Krishna's own being.

gita-13-20.plain: Krishna explains that Matter (nature, called Prakriti) and Spirit (called Purusha) both have no beginning. All changes and all qualities in the world come from Matter.

gita-13-21.plain: Matter is what produces the body, the senses and all causes and effects. Spirit is what experiences pleasure and pain.
themes: why I feel pain and pleasure

gita-13-22.plain: The Spirit lives in the body and experiences the qualities that come from nature. Because it gets attached to those qualities, it is born again and again, sometimes in good lives and sometimes in bad ones.
themes: why am I stuck in patterns

gita-13-23.plain: Inside this body lives the supreme Spirit. It watches, gives permission, supports and experiences. It is called the great Lord and the supreme Self.

gita-13-24.plain: Krishna says that whoever truly understands Spirit and Matter and its qualities will not be born again. This is true whatever kind of life that person is living.

gita-13-25.plain: People find the Self in different ways. Some see it within themselves through meditation. Others reach it through the path of knowledge, called Sankhya, and others through selfless action.
themes: which path is right for me

gita-13-26.plain: Some people do not know these paths themselves. They learn about them from others and worship with faith. They too go beyond death by holding firmly to what they heard.

gita-13-27.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that every creature that is born, whether it moves or stays still, comes from the joining of the Field (matter) and the Knower of the Field (spirit).

gita-13-28.plain: The supreme Lord lives equally in every being. It never dies, even when bodies die. Whoever sees this truly sees.

gita-13-29.plain: Whoever sees the same Lord living equally everywhere does not harm his own true Self. Such a person walks the highest path.

gita-13-30.plain: Whoever sees that nature does all actions, and that the true Self does not act, sees truly.

gita-13-31.plain: When a person sees that all the different beings come from One source and grow out of it, that person reaches the Eternal, Brahman.

gita-6-28.plain: Krishna says that a yogi (a person who practices meditation and inner discipline) who keeps calming and balancing himself becomes free of wrongdoing. Such a person easily feels the endless joy of being in touch with the Eternal, meaning God.

gita-6-29.plain: Krishna says that a person made calm and balanced by yoga sees the same divine Self living inside every being. He sees all beings as part of that one Self, so he sees the same thing everywhere.

gita-6-30.plain: Krishna says that whoever sees Him everywhere and sees everything as resting in Him will never be lost to Him. Krishna will never let go of that person, and that person will never lose Krishna.
themes: fear of being abandoned by God

gita-6-31.plain: Krishna says that a person who feels at one with everything and worships Him as living in all beings truly lives in Him. This is true however that person lives their daily life.
themes: living with faith at work or home

gita-6-32.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that the perfect yogi feels others' joy and pain as if it were his own. Because he sees himself in everyone, he treats all beings equally, whether in pleasure or in pain.

gita-6-33.plain: Arjuna tells Krishna, whom he calls Madhusudana (slayer of the demon Madhu), that he cannot see how this yoga of staying calm and balanced could last. His mind is too restless to stay steady.
themes: feeling spiritual goals are too hard

gita-6-34.plain: Arjuna says the mind is restless, wild, strong and stubborn. He thinks controlling it is as hard as trying to hold back the wind.

gita-6-35.plain: Krishna agrees that the mind is restless and hard to control. But he says it can be controlled through steady, repeated practice and by letting go of cravings.

gita-6-36.plain: Krishna says yoga is very hard for someone with no self-control. But a person who disciplines himself can reach it by putting his effort in the right direction.

gita-6-37.plain: Arjuna asks about a person who has faith but lacks self-control, whose mind wanders away from yoga so they never reach the goal. What happens to that person?

gita-6-38.plain: Arjuna worries that such a person loses out on both worldly life and spiritual success. He asks if they simply fade away like a torn cloud, lost on the path to God.

gita-6-39.plain: Arjuna begs Krishna to clear away this doubt completely. He says no one but Krishna is able to answer it.

gita-6-40.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, the son of Pritha, that such a person is never destroyed, not in this life or the next. Anyone who does good never ends up on a path of misery.

gita-6-41.plain: Krishna explains that the person who fell away from yoga goes to the heavenly worlds of good people and stays there a very long time. Then they are born again into a good and fortunate family.

gita-6-42.plain: Krishna says such a person might even be born into a family of wise yogis. But he adds that a birth like that is very rare in this world.
themes: growing up in a spiritual family

gita-6-43.plain: Krishna says that in the new life, the person gets back the spiritual progress they made before. With it, they work toward perfection once again.

gita-6-44.plain: Krishna says the habits from that earlier practice pull the person strongly back to the spiritual path. Even someone who only wants to learn about yoga goes beyond simply following religious rituals.

gita-6-45.plain: Krishna says the yogi who keeps working hard and is cleansed of wrongdoing becomes fully perfect over many lifetimes. In the end, they reach the highest goal.

gita-6-46.plain: Krishna says the yogi is greater than people who only punish their bodies, greater than the merely learned, and greater than people who only do rituals and duties. So he tells Arjuna to become a yogi.

gita-6-47.plain: Krishna says that of all yogis, the best is the one full of faith who keeps their inner self fixed on Him and worships Him with love. Krishna sees that person as the most united with Him.

gita-17-6.plain: Krishna continues: people who harshly punish their own bodies for show or out of pride are foolish. They hurt the body, and they also hurt Krishna, who lives within them. Their aims are cruel and wrong.

gita-17-7.plain: Krishna says that the food people like comes in three kinds, matching the three qualities of nature: pure, passionate and dark. The same is true of worship, self-discipline and giving to others. He is about to explain each one.
themes: what my choices say about me

gita-17-8.plain: Pure, calm people like food that gives life, strength, health and happiness. Their food is tasty, mild, filling and pleasant to eat.

gita-17-9.plain: Restless, passionate people crave food that is very bitter, sour, salty, spicy, dry or burning. This kind of food leads to pain, unhappiness and sickness.

gita-17-10.plain: Dull, lazy people like food that is stale, tasteless, rotten, leftover or dirty.

gita-17-11.plain: Worship or offering is pure when people do it the right way simply because it is their duty, without wanting anything back.

gita-17-12.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that worship done to get a reward or to look good in front of others comes from passion and selfish desire.

gita-17-13.plain: Worship is dark and empty when it ignores the proper rules, shares no food with others, leaves out the sacred words, gives no gifts to the priests, and has no faith behind it.

gita-17-14.plain: Self-discipline of the body means respecting God, holy people, teachers and wise people. It also means being clean, honest, sexually self-controlled and never hurting anyone.

gita-17-15.plain: Self-discipline of speech means saying things that are true, kind and helpful and that do not upset others. It also includes regularly reading and reciting holy books.

gita-17-16.plain: Self-discipline of the mind means keeping a calm, cheerful mind. It also means being balanced, quiet inside, in control of yourself, and pure in heart.

gita-17-17.plain: When people practice these three disciplines of body, speech and mind with deep faith, a steady mind, and no wish for reward, their practice is pure.

gita-17-18.plain: Discipline done to win respect, praise or attention, or to show off, comes from passion. Its good effects do not last.

gita-17-19.plain: Discipline done out of confusion, by torturing yourself, or in order to harm someone else is the darkest kind.

gita-17-20.plain: A gift is pure when it is given because giving is right, to a worthy person, at the right time and place, and to someone who cannot repay you.

gita-17-21.plain: A gift comes from passion when it is given to get something back, to win a reward, or when it is given unwillingly.

gita-17-22.plain: A gift is dark when it is given at the wrong time or place, to the wrong person, or with rudeness and contempt.

gita-17-23.plain: Krishna says the three words "Om Tat Sat" are a sacred name for God, the Eternal. Long ago, priests, holy books and acts of worship all came from this.

gita-17-24.plain: Because of this, people who know God always begin their worship, giving and self-discipline by saying "Om," the most sacred sound.

gita-17-25.plain: People who want to be free from the cycle of rebirth say "Tat," meaning "That," a word for God. Then they do their worship, discipline and giving without wanting any reward.

gita-18-78.plain: Sanjaya, the narrator telling this story to the blind King Dhritarashtra, ends with his own opinion. He says that wherever Krishna, the master of yoga, stands together with Arjuna (called Partha, son of Pritha), the great archer, there will surely be good fortune, victory and happiness.

gita-18-58.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that if he keeps his mind on Krishna, God's help will carry him past every difficulty. But if pride makes him refuse to listen, he will ruin himself completely.

gita-18-59.plain: Krishna says that Arjuna's pride makes him think, "I will not fight." That decision will not hold, because his own nature as a warrior will push him to act anyway.
themes: you can't escape who you are

gita-18-60.plain: Krishna, calling Arjuna "son of Kunti" (his mother), says that Arjuna is tied to the duty that comes from his own nature. What he now refuses to do out of confusion, he will end up doing anyway, without choice.

gita-18-61.plain: Krishna says that God lives in the heart of every living being. With His mysterious power, He moves all beings around, as if they were riding on a spinning potter's wheel.

gita-18-62.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, whom he calls "Bharata" (descendant of King Bharata), to run to God for safety with his whole heart. Through God's kindness he will find the deepest peace and a lasting home.

gita-18-63.plain: Krishna says he has now shared wisdom more secret than any secret. He tells Arjuna to think it over carefully and then choose for himself what to do.

gita-18-64.plain: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen once more to his highest and most secret teaching. He says he is sharing it because Arjuna is dearly loved and steady in heart.

gita-18-65.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to fill his mind with Krishna, love him, offer worship to him, and bow to him. Krishna promises that Arjuna will surely come to him, because Arjuna is dear to him.

gita-18-66.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to let go of every other duty and come to him alone for shelter. He says not to worry, because he will free Arjuna from all his sins.

gita-18-67.plain: Krishna warns Arjuna not to share this teaching with people who have no self-discipline, no devotion, no wish to listen, or who speak badly of Krishna.

gita-18-68.plain: Krishna says that anyone who lovingly teaches this highest secret to other devotees will surely come to him.

gita-18-69.plain: Krishna says no one does him a dearer service than the person who shares this teaching, and no one on earth will be more loved by him.

gita-18-70.plain: Krishna says that whoever studies this sacred conversation between him and Arjuna is worshipping him through the offering of knowledge.

gita-18-71.plain: Krishna says even someone who simply listens to this teaching with faith, without mocking it, will be freed from wrongdoing and reach the bright worlds of good people.

gita-18-72.plain: Krishna asks Arjuna, calling him "son of Pritha" and "Dhananjaya" (winner of wealth), whether he listened with full attention. He asks if Arjuna's confusion, caused by lack of understanding, is now gone.

gita-18-73.plain: Arjuna answers that his confusion is gone and he understands now, thanks to Krishna's kindness. He feels steady, his doubts are gone, and he will do what Krishna says.

gita-18-74.plain: Sanjaya, the narrator telling the story to the blind king, says he heard this amazing conversation between Krishna (Vasudeva) and the great Arjuna (Partha), and it made his hair stand on end.

gita-18-75.plain: Sanjaya says that by the gift of the sage Vyasa, who gave him special sight, he heard this secret, highest teaching straight from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, as if right before his eyes.

gita-18-76.plain: Sanjaya tells the king that each time he remembers this wonderful, holy conversation between Krishna (Keshava) and Arjuna, he feels joy again and again.

gita-18-77.plain: Sanjaya says that each time he remembers Krishna's amazing universal form (Hari is a name of Krishna), he is filled with great wonder and keeps rejoicing.

gita-3-22.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (here called Pārtha, son of Pritha) that there is nothing in all the worlds he needs to do and nothing he still needs to gain. Even so, he keeps on working.
themes: why work if you have everything

gita-3-23.plain: Krishna says that if he ever stopped working, people everywhere would copy him. They watch what he does and follow it.

gita-3-24.plain: Krishna says the worlds would fall apart if he stopped acting. He would cause social disorder, including the mixing up of castes (the traditional social groups), and he would bring harm to all beings.

gita-3-25.plain: Krishna says foolish people work hard because they want the results. Wise people should work just as hard, but without craving results, and for the good of the world.

gita-3-26.plain: Krishna says a wise person should not confuse simple people who are attached to their work. Instead, the wise person should work in tune with God and show by example that good work is worth doing.

gita-3-27.plain: Krishna says all actions are really carried out by the forces of nature, which he calls the qualities. But a person fooled by ego thinks, "I am the one doing it."

gita-3-28.plain: Krishna says the person who truly understands how nature's qualities work sees that they are only acting on each other. So this person does not get attached.

gita-3-29.plain: Krishna says people fooled by nature's qualities get attached to what those qualities do. Someone who fully understands should not upset people who understand less.

gita-3-30.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to offer all his actions to him and keep his mind on the highest Self. Free of selfish hopes, ego and anxious feverish worry, he should fight.

gita-3-31.plain: Krishna says people who follow this teaching steadily, with faith and without picking fault, are also freed from the binding effects of their actions.

gita-3-32.plain: Krishna says people who mock his teaching and do not follow it are confused and lack understanding. He warns that they are headed for ruin.

gita-3-33.plain: Krishna says even a wise person acts according to their own nature. All beings follow their nature, so just forcing yourself to hold back does not achieve much.

gita-3-34.plain: Krishna says the senses naturally feel liking for some things and dislike for others. No one should let these likes and dislikes take control, because they block the spiritual path.

gita-3-35.plain: Krishna says it is better to do your own duty, even poorly, than to do someone else's duty well. It is better even to die doing your own duty, because following another's path is full of danger.

gita-3-36.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna (here called Vārshneya, of the Vrishni clan) what pushes a person to do wrong, even when they do not want to, as if they were forced.
themes: why do I do wrong things
doing what I know is bad

gita-3-37.plain: Krishna answers that it is desire, and the anger that comes from it. They arise from the restless quality of nature, are never satisfied, cause great harm, and are our enemy in this world.

gita-3-38.plain: Krishna says desire covers wisdom the way smoke covers a fire, dust covers a mirror, and the womb's covering surrounds an unborn baby.

gita-3-39.plain: Krishna says desire is the constant enemy of wise people. It hides their wisdom, and like a fire it is never satisfied.

gita-3-40.plain: Krishna says desire lives in the senses, the mind and the thinking intellect. Through them it hides wisdom and confuses the soul living in the body.

gita-3-41.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to first take control of his senses. Then he should destroy desire, the source of wrongdoing that ruins wisdom and understanding.

gita-15-10.plain: Krishna says that people confused by their desires and moods do not notice the soul inside the body, whether it is staying, leaving at death, or enjoying the senses. Only people with the eye of wisdom can see it.
themes: why some people don't understand spiritual things

gita-15-11.plain: Krishna says that people who practice yoga and work hard at it, staying centered in their true self, do see the soul. But people who have not trained their minds do not see it, even when they try.

gita-15-12.plain: Krishna says the light of the sun that lights up the whole world, and the light in the moon and in fire, all come from him.

gita-15-13.plain: Krishna says he enters the earth and holds up all living things with his energy. He also becomes Soma, a life-giving juice, and feeds all the plants.

gita-15-14.plain: Krishna says he lives inside every breathing body as the fire of digestion. Working with the breath, he digests the four kinds of food people eat.

gita-15-15.plain: Krishna says he lives in the heart of every being. Memory and wisdom, and also forgetting, come from him. He is what all the Vedas, the holy books, aim to teach, and he is the one who wrote and truly knows them.

gita-15-16.plain: Krishna says there are two kinds of being in the world. All living creatures are perishable, and the unchanging part behind them is called imperishable.

gita-15-17.plain: Krishna says there is a highest being beyond both of these, called the Supreme Self. This Lord fills everything, holds up all three worlds, and never perishes.

gita-15-18.plain: Krishna says that because he is greater than both the perishable and the imperishable, the world and the holy books call him the Supreme Person.

gita-15-19.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that whoever clearly knows him as the Supreme Person knows everything that matters. That person worships him with their whole heart and life.

gita-15-20.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, whom he calls pure, that he has now shared this most secret teaching. Whoever understands it becomes wise and has done what life is for.

gita-16-1.plain: Krishna starts listing the good qualities of a godly person: being fearless, living cleanly, staying steady in seeking wisdom, giving to others, self-control, making offerings, studying scripture, simple self-discipline, and honesty.
themes: how to be a good person

gita-16-2.plain: Krishna continues the list: not hurting anyone, telling the truth, not getting angry, letting go, being peaceful, not scheming, kindness to all living things, not being greedy, gentleness, modesty, and not being restless or changeable.

gita-16-3.plain: Krishna finishes the list: energy, forgiveness, endurance, purity, and freedom from jealousy and pride. He says these belong to a person born with godly qualities.

gita-16-4.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna the qualities of a person born with demonic, or harmful, nature: faking goodness, arrogance, being full of oneself, anger, harshness, and foolishness.

gita-16-5.plain: Krishna says godly qualities lead to freedom, and demonic qualities keep a person trapped. He comforts Arjuna: do not worry, you were born with godly qualities.

gita-16-6.plain: Krishna says there are two kinds of beings in this world, godly and demonic. He has already described the godly kind in detail, and now he will describe the demonic kind.

gita-16-7.plain: Krishna says demonic people do not know when to act and when to hold back. They have no purity, no good manners, and no truthfulness.

gita-16-8.plain: Krishna says such people claim the universe has no truth, no foundation, and no God. They say it came about only by chance mating, driven by desire and nothing else.

gita-16-9.plain: Krishna says people who hold this view are lost and narrow-minded. They do cruel things and become enemies who bring harm and destruction to the world.
themes: how bad beliefs lead to harm

gita-3-42.plain: Krishna says the senses are powerful, the mind is stronger than the senses, and reason (our power to judge and decide) is stronger than the mind. But stronger than reason is the true Self, the divine presence within.

gita-3-43.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to know that his true Self is higher than his thinking mind. Using that higher Self to steady his lower self, he should defeat desire, an enemy that is very hard to beat.

gita-4-1.plain: Krishna says he first taught this lasting teaching of yoga to Vivasvan, the sun god. Vivasvan taught it to Manu, the first man, and Manu taught it to King Ikshvaku.

gita-4-2.plain: Krishna says wise kings passed this teaching down from one to the next. But over a very long time it was lost in the world.

gita-4-3.plain: Krishna says he is now teaching this same old wisdom to Arjuna. He shares this highest secret because Arjuna loves him and is his friend.

gita-4-4.plain: Arjuna is puzzled. He asks how Krishna could have taught the sun god long ago, when Krishna was born much later.

gita-4-5.plain: Krishna answers that both he and Arjuna have been born many times before. Krishna remembers all his past lives, but Arjuna does not remember his.

gita-4-6.plain: Krishna explains that he is never truly born and never dies, and he is the Lord of all beings. Still, he takes birth in the world by his own divine power, working through nature, which belongs to him.

gita-4-7.plain: Krishna says that whenever goodness weakens and wrongdoing grows strong in the world, he comes into the world himself.
themes: why is there so much evil

gita-4-8.plain: Krishna says he is born again and again, in age after age. He comes to protect good people, to destroy those who do evil, and to set goodness firmly in place again.

gita-4-9.plain: Krishna says anyone who truly understands his divine birth and work is not born again after death. That person comes to Krishna instead.

gita-4-10.plain: Krishna says many people have reached him. They were free from strong desire, fear, and anger. Their minds were full of him and they relied on him, and wisdom made them pure.

gita-4-11.plain: Krishna says that however people come to him, he welcomes them in that same way. Every path people take, from every direction, leads to him.

gita-4-12.plain: Krishna says people who want success in worldly things pray to the gods, the Shining Ones. In this world, such work brings results quickly.

gita-4-13.plain: Krishna says he created the four groups of people in society, based on each person's nature and the work they do. He made them, yet he himself does not act and never changes.

gita-4-14.plain: Krishna says actions do not bind him, and he does not want anything from their results. A person who understands this about him is not trapped by their own actions either.

gita-4-15.plain: Krishna says the wise people of long ago knew this and kept working while seeking spiritual freedom. So Arjuna should also do his work, as they did.
themes: should I quit or keep going

gita-4-16.plain: Krishna says even wise people get confused about what counts as action and what counts as not acting. He promises to explain it, so that Arjuna can be free from wrongdoing.

gita-4-17.plain: Krishna says a person must understand three things: right action, wrong action, and not acting. He says the way action works is hard to understand.

gita-4-18.plain: Krishna says a truly wise person sees that there can be stillness inside activity, and activity inside stillness. Such a person stays balanced and at peace even while doing all kinds of work.

gita-6-8.plain: Krishna says a yogi (a person who practices yoga, the discipline of joining the mind with God) is content with what he knows and understands. He stays steady, controls his senses, and sees a lump of dirt, a stone and gold as having the same worth.

gita-6-9.plain: Krishna says the best person treats everyone the same: friends, enemies, strangers, family, people who don't care either way, and good and bad people alike.

gita-6-10.plain: Krishna says the yogi should practice meditation regularly, alone in a quiet, private place. He should keep his mind and body under control and let go of wanting and grasping.

gita-6-11.plain: Krishna describes the meditation seat. It should be in a clean place, firm, not too high and not too low, made of kusha grass (a sacred grass), with a deer skin and then a cloth on top.

gita-6-12.plain: Krishna says to sit steadily on that seat and focus the mind on one thing. With thoughts and senses calmed, a person should meditate to make the inner self pure.

gita-6-13.plain: Krishna says to keep the body, head and neck straight and still. The eyes rest toward the tip of the nose without looking around at anything.

gita-6-14.plain: Krishna says the meditator should be calm and unafraid, and keep the vow of a brahmachari (a student who lives a pure, celibate life). With the mind controlled, he should sit thinking of Krishna and longing for Him.

gita-6-15.plain: Krishna says the yogi who always keeps his mind controlled and joined with the Self reaches peace. This is the highest joy, which lives in Krishna.

gita-6-16.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that yoga does not work for someone who eats too much or too little. It also does not work for someone who sleeps too much or too little.

gita-6-17.plain: Krishna says yoga removes all suffering for a person who is balanced. Such a person is moderate in eating, fun, work, sleep and waking.

gita-6-18.plain: Krishna says a person is called balanced when his calm mind rests on the Self and he no longer craves the things people usually want.

gita-6-19.plain: Krishna says the mind of a yogi deep in meditation is like a lamp flame in a place with no wind. It does not flicker.

gita-6-20.plain: Krishna describes the state where the mind finally rests, made quiet by meditation. In it, a person sees his true Self and is fully satisfied within.

gita-6-21.plain: Krishna says in that state a person finds the greatest joy. This joy goes beyond the senses and is known by the understanding. Once there, he does not slip away from what is truly real.

gita-6-22.plain: Krishna says once someone reaches this state, he knows nothing is worth more. Even a great sorrow cannot shake him.

gita-6-23.plain: Krishna says yoga means being cut off from pain. A person should stick with this practice firmly and without losing heart.

gita-6-24.plain: Krishna says to completely drop the desires that come from imagining things. Use the mind to pull back all the senses from every direction.

gita-6-25.plain: Krishna says to grow calm slowly, step by step, using steady understanding. Once the mind rests in the Self, think of nothing else.

gita-6-26.plain: Krishna says the mind is restless and wanders. Every time it wanders off, bring it back and place it under the control of the Self.

gita-6-27.plain: Krishna says the highest joy comes to the yogi whose mind is peaceful and whose strong passions have calmed down. Such a person is free of sin and has become one with the Eternal.

gita-8-11.plain: Krishna says he will briefly describe the path to the eternal reality. Scholars of the Vedas (the ancient holy texts) call it indestructible. Self-controlled people who are free of craving reach it, and people live a disciplined, celibate student life (Brahmacharya) because they want it.

gita-8-12.plain: Krishna describes how a yogi prepares at the moment of death. He shuts the doors of the senses, holds his mind still in the heart, gathers his life-breath up into his head, and stays focused through yoga.

gita-8-13.plain: Whoever leaves the body while saying "Om," the one sacred syllable that stands for the Eternal, and while thinking of Krishna, goes on the highest path.
themes: what to think about when dying
prayer at the end of life

gita-8-14.plain: Krishna says that a person who thinks of him all the time, and never lets the mind drift to other things, reaches him easily. Arjuna is called Partha here, meaning son of Pritha.

gita-8-15.plain: Great souls who reach Krishna are never born again into this world. This world is full of pain and does not last. They have reached the highest joy.

gita-8-16.plain: Krishna says every world, even the heaven of Brahma the creator god, appears and then passes away. But a person who reaches Krishna is never born again.
themes: nothing in this world is permanent
the cycle of life and death

gita-8-17.plain: Krishna explains cosmic time. One day of Brahma, the creator, lasts a thousand great ages, and his night lasts just as long. People who understand this truly know what day and night mean.

gita-8-18.plain: When Brahma's day begins, all visible things flow out of the hidden, unseen source. When his night comes, they all melt back into that unseen source.
themes: how the universe begins and ends

gita-8-19.plain: All living beings come into existence again and again. They dissolve when the cosmic night comes and appear again when the day comes. This happens by a fixed law, not by their own choice.
themes: the cycle of birth and death

gita-8-20.plain: Beyond that unseen source of the universe there is a higher unseen reality. It is eternal, and it is not destroyed even when all beings are destroyed.
themes: what survives the end of everything

gita-8-21.plain: That higher unseen reality is called the Indestructible and the highest goal. Those who reach it never come back to this world. Krishna says it is his own supreme home.

gita-8-22.plain: The highest Spirit can be reached through steady love and devotion to him alone. All beings live inside him, and he fills the whole universe.
themes: devotion as the way to God

gita-8-23.plain: Krishna says he will now explain two kinds of times for leaving the body. Yogis who die at one time do not return to this world. Those who die at the other time do return.

gita-8-24.plain: Krishna names the bright path: fire, light, daytime, the waxing moon, and the six months when the sun moves north. People who know the Eternal and die on this path go to the Eternal and do not return.

gita-8-25.plain: Krishna names the dark path: smoke, night, the waning moon, and the six months when the sun moves south. A yogi who dies on this path reaches the light of the moon, and then he comes back to be born again.

gita-8-26.plain: Light and darkness are the two lasting paths of the world. One leads to freedom with no return. The other leads back to birth again.

gita-8-27.plain: A yogi who knows these two paths is never confused. So Krishna tells Arjuna to stay steady in yoga at all times.

gita-8-28.plain: The Vedas promise rewards for rituals, hard self-discipline, and giving to charity. A yogi who understands this teaching goes beyond all those rewards and reaches the supreme, ancient home of God.

gita-9-1.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that because he does not find fault or argue, he will share the deepest secret with him. It is wisdom joined with practical knowledge, and knowing it will free Arjuna from evil.

gita-9-2.plain: Krishna calls this teaching the king of all knowledge and the king of all secrets. It purifies more than anything else. A person can sense its truth directly. It fits with what is right, it is very easy to practice, and it never fades.
themes: truth you can feel for yourself

gita-5-17.plain: Krishna says that people who keep their minds on God, give themselves fully to God and rest in God reach a state they never fall back from. Their wisdom has washed away their wrongs.
themes: wanting to be free of past mistakes

gita-5-18.plain: Krishna says that wise people see the same worth in everyone and everything. A learned and humble priest (Brahmana), a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a person society rejects as an outcaste all look equal to them.
themes: seeing the sacred in all beings

gita-5-19.plain: Krishna says that people whose minds stay calm and fair toward all have already won over life, even while living on earth. God, the Eternal, is pure and the same toward everyone, so people who are balanced like that live in God.

gita-5-20.plain: Krishna says that a person who truly knows God has a steady mind and is not confused. They do not get overexcited when good things happen or crushed when bad things happen.
themes: staying steady in good and bad times
not getting carried away by success

gita-5-21.plain: Krishna says that a person who does not cling to outside pleasures finds joy inside, in their true self. Through yoga, meaning practice that joins the mind to God, they feel a happiness that never ends.
themes: depending on outside things for happiness

gita-5-22.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Kaunteya, son of Kunti) that pleasures from the senses lead to pain. They start and they end, so a wise person does not build happiness on them.

gita-5-23.plain: Krishna says that a person who can hold back the strong push of desire and anger, while still alive in this body, is balanced and truly happy.

gita-5-24.plain: Krishna says that the yogi, a person who practices joining with God, whose happiness, joy and light come from within, becomes one with God and reaches God's peace.

gita-5-25.plain: Krishna says that sages (rishis) reach God's peace when their wrongs are gone, they no longer see the world split into opposites, they control themselves, and they work for the good of all living beings.

gita-5-26.plain: Krishna says that God's peace is close to people who know their true selves, who are free from desire and anger, and who keep their nature and thoughts under control.

gita-5-27.plain: Krishna begins describing meditation. Shut out the outside world, rest your gaze between the eyebrows, and make your breathing in and out through the nose even and calm.

gita-5-28.plain: Krishna continues: the sage who keeps their senses, mind and understanding under control, who wants only freedom, and who has dropped desire, fear and anger for good, is truly free.

gita-5-29.plain: Krishna says that a person who knows him finds peace. They know him as the one who receives every offering and every hard spiritual practice, the great ruler of all the worlds, and the loving friend of every being.

gita-6-1.plain: Krishna says the real holy person is someone who does their duty without caring about the reward. Someone is not holy just because they stopped lighting the sacred fire and doing religious rituals.

gita-6-2.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Pandava, son of Pandu) that giving things up and yoga are really the same. No one becomes a true yogi without giving up their selfish plans and wants.

gita-6-3.plain: Krishna says that for someone just starting on the path of yoga, doing good work is the way forward. Once they are settled in yoga, staying calm and peaceful becomes the way forward.

gita-6-4.plain: Krishna says a person is settled in yoga when they no longer cling to pleasures or to their actions. They have given up their selfish plans and wants.

gita-6-5.plain: Krishna says you must lift yourself up with your own higher self and not let yourself sink down. Your own mind can be your best friend or your worst enemy.

gita-6-6.plain: Krishna says that when you have mastered yourself, your higher self is your friend. When you have not, your own self works against you like an enemy.

gita-6-7.plain: Krishna says that a person who has mastered themselves and is at peace stays steady with God. Cold or heat, pleasure or pain, praise or insult do not shake them.

gita-10-9.plain: Krishna describes people who love God. They keep their minds on Him and give their lives to Him. They help each other understand and always enjoy talking about Him, and this makes them happy and at peace.

gita-10-10.plain: Krishna says that to people who stay steady and worship Him with love, He gives the wisdom to tell what is real from what is not. This understanding leads them to Him.

gita-10-11.plain: Krishna says that out of kindness, He lives inside the hearts of those who love Him. There He drives away the darkness of not knowing, like a bright lamp lighting up a dark room.

gita-10-12.plain: Arjuna praises Krishna. He calls Him the highest eternal Being, the final home of all, perfectly pure, the first God, never born, and the Lord of all.

gita-10-13.plain: Arjuna says that the great sages, called Rishis, have all said this about Krishna. Famous wise men like Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa said it too, and now Krishna Himself is telling him.

gita-10-14.plain: Arjuna tells Krishna, here called Keshava, that he believes everything Krishna has said. He adds that neither the gods nor the demons, called Danavas, truly understand who Krishna is.

gita-10-15.plain: Arjuna says that only Krishna truly knows Himself. He calls Krishna the Supreme Person (Purushottama), the source and ruler of all beings, God of the gods, and Lord of the world.

gita-10-16.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna to tell him fully about His divine glories. These are the powers by which Krishna fills and lives in all the worlds.

gita-10-17.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna how he can come to know Him by always thinking of Him. He wants to know in what forms or things he should think of Krishna.

gita-10-18.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna, called Janardana, to explain His power and glory again in detail. He says he never gets tired of hearing Krishna's words, which give him life.

gita-10-19.plain: Krishna blesses Arjuna and agrees to tell him about His divine glory. But He says He will only name the main examples, because there is no end to them.

gita-10-20.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, called Gudakesha, that He is the Self living in the heart of every being. He is the beginning, the middle, and the end of all living things.

gita-10-21.plain: Krishna begins listing the best things in which He shows Himself. Among the sky gods called Adityas, He is Vishnu. Among lights, He is the sun. Among the storm gods called Maruts, He is Marichi. Among the stars at night, He is the moon.
themes: God in the best of everything

gita-10-22.plain: Krishna says that among the holy books called Vedas, He is the Sama Veda, the book of sacred songs. Among the gods, He is Indra (Vasava). Among the senses, He is the mind. In living beings, He is the power of awareness and intelligence.

gita-10-23.plain: Krishna says that among the Rudras, gods of storm and change, He is Shankara (Shiva). Among nature spirits and giants, He is Kubera (Vittesha), lord of wealth. Among the Vasus, gods of the elements, He is fire. Among tall mountains, He is the sacred Mount Meru.

gita-10-24.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, called Partha, that among priests He is Brihaspati, the chief priest of the gods. Among army leaders, He is Skanda, the war god. Among bodies of water, He is the ocean.

gita-10-25.plain: Krishna says that among great sages He is Bhrigu. Among words, He is the one sacred syllable Om. Among offerings, He is the quiet repeating of a holy name or prayer. Among things that do not move, He is the Himalaya mountains.

gita-10-26.plain: Krishna says that among trees He is the sacred fig tree (Ashvattha). Among divine sages, He is Narada. Among heavenly musicians (Gandharvas), He is Chitraratha. Among perfect beings, He is the sage Kapila.

gita-10-27.plain: Krishna says that among horses He is Uchchaishravas, the heavenly horse born when the ocean was churned for nectar. Among royal elephants, He is Airavata. Among people, He is the king.

gita-10-28.plain: Krishna says that among weapons He is the thunderbolt. Among cows, He is Kamadhuk, the magic cow that grants every wish. Among those who create life, He is Kandarpa, the god of love. Among serpents, He is Vasuki, the serpent king.
themes: God in love and new life

gita-10-29.plain: Krishna keeps naming the best of each group to show where God can be seen. Among serpents he is Ananta, the endless snake. Among sea beings he is Varuna, god of the waters. Among ancestors he is Aryaman, and among those who judge he is Yama, the lord of death.

gita-10-30.plain: Krishna says that among the Daityas, a race of demons, he is Prahlada, a boy famous for his devotion to God. Among things that measure, he is Time. Among wild animals he is the lion, and among birds he is Garuda (Vainateya), the great eagle who carries Vishnu.

gita-10-31.plain: Krishna says that among things that make clean, he is the wind. Among warriors he is Rama, the hero king. Among sea creatures he is the Makara, a great sea animal, and among rivers he is the Ganga, India's holy river.

gita-10-32.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is the beginning, middle and end of everything that is made. Of all kinds of learning, he is the knowledge of the Self, our true inner being. In people who speak well, he is the reasoning in their speech.

gita-10-33.plain: Krishna says he is the letter A, the first sound of the alphabet. In grammar he is the joining of two equal words. He is endless Time. He is the one who holds everything up and sees in every direction.

gita-10-34.plain: Krishna says he is death, which takes everyone, and also the source of everything yet to be born. He is also seen in good qualities: a good name, wealth, fine speech, memory, intelligence, steadiness and patience.

gita-10-35.plain: Krishna says among sacred songs he is the Brihat Saman, a great hymn. Among poem rhythms he is the Gayatri, a holy chant. Among months he is Margashirsha, in late autumn, and among seasons he is spring, the season of flowers.

gita-10-36.plain: Krishna says he is even the gambling of cheaters, the most powerful form of trickery. He is the shine in shining things. He is victory, firm effort, and the goodness in good people.
themes: God in everything, even bad things

gita-10-37.plain: Krishna says among his own family clan, the Vrishnis, he is Vasudeva, meaning Krishna himself. Among the Pandava brothers he is Arjuna (Dhananjaya). Among wise men he is Vyasa, the great sage, and among poets he is Ushana, a famous wise poet.

gita-10-38.plain: Krishna says he is the power of rulers to punish and keep order. In people who want to win, he is good planning. Among secrets he is silence. In wise people he is their wisdom.

gita-10-39.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna he is the seed from which every living being comes. Nothing at all, moving or still, can exist without him.
