gita-10-40.plain: Krishna says his divine powers have no end. What he has listed is only a small sample of his endless greatness.

gita-10-41.plain: Krishna says that anything great, good, beautiful or powerful comes from just a small spark of his glory.

gita-10-42.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna he does not need all these details. It is enough to know that Krishna holds up the whole universe with just one small part of himself, and still remains beyond it.

gita-11-1.plain: Arjuna says that Krishna kindly shared this deepest secret about the Self. Because of it, Arjuna's confusion is gone.

gita-11-2.plain: Arjuna says he has heard in detail from Krishna how all beings are born and die. He has also heard about Krishna's greatness, which never ends.

gita-11-3.plain: Arjuna says he believes what Krishna has told him about himself. Now he wants to actually see Krishna's all-powerful divine form.

gita-11-4.plain: Arjuna humbly asks Krishna, the master of yoga, to show him his eternal form, but only if Krishna thinks Arjuna is able to see it.

gita-11-5.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (Partha) to look at his divine forms. There are hundreds and thousands of them, in many kinds, colors and shapes.

gita-11-6.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to see many groups of gods in him, such as the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the twin Ashvins and the storm gods called Maruts. He will see many wonders no one has seen before.

gita-1-21.plain: Arjuna, the warrior prince, asks Krishna, who is driving his chariot, to stop it in the open space between the two armies. Hrishikesha and Achyuta are names for Krishna.
themes: Arjuna asks to see the enemy

gita-1-22.plain: Arjuna says he wants to look at the people on the other side who are eager to fight. These are the people he will have to battle in this war.
themes: wanting to see who you're up against

gita-1-23.plain: Arjuna wants to see everyone who has come to fight for Duryodhana, the cruel son of King Dhritarashtra. They want to please him by fighting.

gita-1-24.plain: Sanjaya, who is telling the story to the blind King Dhritarashtra, says that Krishna did as Arjuna asked. He drove the fine chariot into the middle, between the two armies. Gudakesha is a name for Arjuna.

gita-1-25.plain: Krishna stops the chariot right in front of Bhishma, Arjuna's great-grandfather figure, and Drona, his old teacher, along with many kings. Krishna says, "Arjuna, look at all these Kurus gathered here." Partha is a name for Arjuna, and the Kurus are his family clan.
themes: facing people you love on the other side
seeing elders and teachers as enemies

gita-1-26.plain: Arjuna looks and sees his own family on the other side. There are uncles, grandfathers, teachers, cousins, sons, grandsons and friends.
themes: shock at seeing loved ones as enemies

gita-1-27.plain: He also sees fathers-in-law and people who had been kind to him, in both armies. Arjuna sees that all of them are his relatives, lined up to fight.
themes: realizing the cost of a fight

gita-1-28.plain: Arjuna is filled with pity and sadness. He tells Krishna that seeing his own family lined up and eager to fight hurts him deeply.

gita-1-29.plain: Arjuna describes what is happening to his body. His legs feel weak, his mouth is dry, he is shaking, and his hair stands on end.

gita-1-30.plain: Arjuna says his bow, called Gandiva, is slipping from his hand. His skin feels like it is burning, he cannot stand, and his mind is spinning.

gita-1-31.plain: Arjuna says he sees bad signs. He cannot see any good coming from killing his own family in battle. Keshava is a name for Krishna.
themes: seeing no point in a fight

gita-1-32.plain: Arjuna tells Krishna he does not want victory, a kingdom or pleasures. He asks what good any of that is, or even life itself, if it costs this much. Govinda is a name for Krishna.
themes: losing the will to go on

gita-1-33.plain: Arjuna says the very people he would want a kingdom and happy life for are the ones standing here, ready to die. Winning would mean nothing without them.
themes: success means nothing without loved ones

gita-1-34.plain: Arjuna lists who is standing there: teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives.

gita-1-35.plain: Arjuna says he does not want to kill them, even if they kill him. He would not do it even to rule all three worlds, so he will certainly not do it for one kingdom on earth. Madhusudana is a name for Krishna.
themes: willing to suffer rather than harm others

gita-1-36.plain: Arjuna asks how they could ever be happy after killing Dhritarashtra's sons. Even though those cousins have done wrong, he says killing them would only bring sin upon himself and his brothers. Janardana is a name for Krishna.

gita-1-37.plain: So Arjuna says they should not kill their cousins. He asks how anyone could be happy after killing their own family. Madhava is a name for Krishna.

gita-1-38.plain: Arjuna says that the other side is blinded by greed. They do not see anything wrong in destroying a family or turning against friends.

gita-1-39.plain: Arjuna asks why he and his brothers, who can see how wrong it is to destroy a family, should not step away from such a sin.

gita-1-40.plain: Arjuna says that when a family is destroyed, its old traditions are lost. When traditions are lost, the family stops following what is right and falls into disorder.

gita-1-1.plain: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks his aide Sanjaya what happened when his sons and their cousins, the Pandavas, gathered to fight on the sacred field of Kurukshetra. Sanjaya has a special gift that lets him see the battle from far away.

gita-1-2.plain: Sanjaya begins his report. Prince Duryodhana, the king's eldest son, sees the Pandava army lined up for battle and goes to speak to his teacher, Drona.
themes: a prince sizes up the enemy

gita-1-3.plain: Duryodhana tells his teacher Drona to look at the huge Pandava army. He points out that it was arranged by the son of Drupada, who was once Drona's own student.
themes: a student now on the other side

gita-1-4.plain: Duryodhana names great archers in the Pandava army who are as strong in battle as Bhima and Arjuna. They include Yuyudhana, Virata and Drupada, who rides a great chariot.

gita-1-5.plain: Duryodhana keeps naming strong warriors on the Pandava side. Among them are the brave King of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaivya, a leader among men.

gita-1-6.plain: He names more Pandava fighters: strong Yudhamanyu and brave Uttamaujas. He also names Abhimanyu, Arjuna's son by Subhadra, and the sons of Draupadi, all mighty chariot warriors.

gita-1-7.plain: Duryodhana now tells his teacher Drona that he will name the main leaders of his own army.

gita-1-8.plain: He names the chief warriors on his side. They are Drona himself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna and the son of Somadatta, all winners in battle.

gita-1-9.plain: Duryodhana says many other skilled heroes are ready to give their lives for him. They carry all kinds of weapons.

gita-1-10.plain: Duryodhana admits a worry. His army, led by the old warrior Bhishma, seems not strong enough, while the Pandava army, guarded by Bhima, seems strong enough.

gita-1-11.plain: So Duryodhana orders all his generals to hold their places in the ranks and protect Bhishma above all.

gita-1-12.plain: To cheer Duryodhana up, the honored old grandfather Bhishma blows his conch shell horn. It sounds loud like a lion's roar.

gita-1-13.plain: Then all at once conch shells, drums and horns blare out on Duryodhana's side. The noise is huge.

gita-1-14.plain: On the other side, Krishna (here called Madhava) and Arjuna stand in their great chariot pulled by white horses. They blow their divine conch shells.

gita-1-15.plain: Krishna blows his conch named Panchajanya, and Arjuna blows his named Devadatta. Bhima, known for fierce deeds, blows his mighty conch Paundra.

gita-1-16.plain: King Yudhishthira, eldest son of Kunti, blows his conch Anantavijaya. The twins Nakula and Sahadeva blow theirs, Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

gita-1-17.plain: The great archer King of Kashi, the mighty chariot warrior Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata and the unbeaten Satyaki also sound their conches.

gita-1-18.plain: Sanjaya tells the king that Drupada, the sons of Draupadi and strong-armed Abhimanyu also blow their conches from every side.

gita-1-19.plain: The huge roar from the Pandava side fills earth and sky. It shakes the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons with fear.

gita-1-20.plain: Arjuna, whose flag shows a monkey, sees Dhritarashtra's sons lined up as the arrows are about to fly. He picks up his bow.
themes: the battle is about to start

gita-18-38.plain: Krishna says some pleasure comes from the senses meeting the things they enjoy. It feels sweet at first but turns bitter, like poison, in the end. He calls this the restless, passionate kind of pleasure.

gita-18-39.plain: Krishna says the lowest, "dark" kind of pleasure fools a person from start to finish. It comes from too much sleep, laziness and carelessness.

gita-18-40.plain: Krishna says no being on earth or in heaven, not even among the gods ("Shining Ones"), is free from the three qualities of nature. These are goodness, restless passion and dullness.
themes: why people act the way they do

gita-18-41.plain: Krishna says the duties of the four social groups of his time were divided according to the natural qualities of each. These groups were priests and teachers (Brahmanas), warriors and rulers (Kshattriyas), farmers and traders (Vaishyas), and workers who serve (Shudras).
themes: what am I meant to do

gita-18-42.plain: Krishna lists the natural duties of a Brahmana, a priest or teacher. They are calmness, self-control, simple living, purity, forgiveness, honesty, wisdom, knowledge and faith in God.

gita-18-43.plain: Krishna lists the natural duties of a Kshattriya, a warrior or ruler. They are courage, strength of spirit, steadiness, skill, not running from battle, generosity and leadership.

gita-18-44.plain: Krishna says the natural work of a Vaishya is farming, caring for cows and trade. The natural work of a Shudra is serving others.

gita-18-45.plain: Krishna says a person reaches perfection by giving themselves fully to their own duty. He then promises to explain how this works.

gita-18-46.plain: Krishna says God is the source of all beings and is present everywhere. A person reaches perfection by worshipping God through doing their own work.

gita-18-47.plain: Krishna says it is better to do your own duty imperfectly than to do someone else's duty well. Doing the work that fits your nature brings no sin.

gita-18-48.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, "son of Kunti," not to give up the duty he was born to, even if it has flaws. Every kind of work has some fault, just as every fire gives off smoke.

gita-18-49.plain: Krishna says a person who is not clinging to anything, who controls themselves and has let go of desires, reaches the highest freedom by letting go.

gita-18-50.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna he will briefly explain how a person who has reached perfection goes on to reach the Eternal, the highest state of wisdom.
themes: next step on the spiritual path

gita-18-51.plain: Krishna begins describing the person ready for the Eternal. They have a clear, pure mind and steady self-control. They turn away from sense pleasures like sounds, and they drop strong likes and dislikes.

gita-18-52.plain: Krishna continues: such a person likes quiet places and eats lightly. They control their speech, body and mind, keep meditating, and stay calm and unattached.

gita-18-53.plain: Krishna says that when a person drops ego, violence, arrogance, desire, anger and greed, and becomes unselfish and peaceful, they are ready to become one with the Eternal.

gita-18-54.plain: Krishna says a person who has become one with the Eternal is calm inside. They no longer grieve or crave. They see all beings as equal and gain the highest love for God.

gita-18-55.plain: Krishna says that through devotion a person truly knows who and what he is. Knowing him this way, they at once enter the Supreme.

gita-18-56.plain: Krishna says that even a person who keeps doing all kinds of work reaches the eternal home that never ends. This happens by his grace, if they take refuge in him.

gita-18-57.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to offer all his work to him in his heart and to stay focused on him. Using wise judgment, he should keep his mind on Krishna always.

gita-7-1.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Pārtha, "son of Prithā") to listen. He will explain how Arjuna can know him fully and without doubt by keeping his mind on Krishna, practicing yoga, and taking shelter in him.

gita-7-2.plain: Krishna promises to teach both knowledge and deep understanding completely. Once Arjuna knows this, nothing else will be left for him to learn.

gita-7-3.plain: Krishna says that out of thousands of people, hardly one really tries for spiritual perfection. Even among those who try and succeed, hardly one truly knows him as he really is.

gita-7-4.plain: Krishna lists eight parts of his nature: earth, water, fire, air, ether (space), mind, reason, and ego (the sense of "I").
themes: what the world is made of

gita-7-5.plain: Krishna says those eight parts are his lower nature. He also has a higher nature, the life force in all living beings, which holds up the whole universe.

gita-7-6.plain: Krishna says his two natures are where all beings come from. He is the source from which the whole universe begins and the place where it ends.
themes: beginning and end of the world

gita-7-7.plain: Krishna, called Dhananjaya's teacher here (Dhananjaya, "winner of wealth," is Arjuna), says nothing is higher than him. Everything is held together by him, like pearls strung on a thread.

gita-7-8.plain: Krishna says he is the taste of water and the light of the moon and sun. He is the sacred syllable Om in the Vedas (holy scriptures), the sound in space, and the strength in men.

gita-7-9.plain: Krishna says he is the sweet smell of the earth and the brightness of fire. He is the life in every being and the self-discipline of those who practice hardship for God.

gita-7-10.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to know him as the eternal seed of all beings. He is the intelligence in the wise and the glory in all glorious things.

gita-7-11.plain: Krishna says he is the strength of the strong when it is free from greed and passion. He is also the desire in people that does not go against what is right.

gita-7-12.plain: Krishna says the three moods of nature—calm goodness, restless activity, and dull laziness—all come from him. They exist within him, but he is not controlled by them.

gita-7-13.plain: Krishna says the whole world is fooled by these three moods of nature. Because of this, people do not recognize him, who is beyond them and never dies.

gita-7-14.plain: Krishna says the illusion made by these three moods is his own divine power, and it is very hard to get past. But those who turn to him get beyond it.

gita-7-15.plain: Krishna says people who do evil, who are foolish, and who are the worst of humans do not come to him. Illusion has taken away their wisdom, and they have taken on a cruel, demon-like nature.

gita-7-16.plain: Krishna says four kinds of good people worship him: those who are suffering, those who want knowledge, those who want something for themselves, and the wise.

gita-7-17.plain: Krishna says the wise person is the best of these four, because they are always steady and devoted to him alone. He is very dear to the wise, and they are very dear to him.
themes: loving God for its own sake

gita-7-18.plain: Krishna says all four kinds of worshippers are good. But he sees the wise one as his very own self, because that person is united within and fixed on him as the highest goal.

gita-7-19.plain: Krishna says that after many lifetimes, the truly wise person comes to him, saying "Vāsudeva (Krishna) is everything." Such a great soul is very hard to find.

gita-7-20.plain: Krishna says people whose understanding is clouded by desires turn to other gods (Shining Ones). They follow various outward rituals, according to their own nature.

gita-13-32.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Kaunteya, son of Kunti) that the highest Self has no beginning and no qualities, and it never dies. Even though it lives inside the body, it does not act and is not touched by what happens.

gita-13-33.plain: Krishna explains that space is everywhere but nothing stains it, because it is so fine. In the same way, the Self is present all through the body but is not affected by it.

gita-13-34.plain: Krishna says that just as one sun lights up the whole earth, the Self, the 'Lord of the Field', lights up the whole body and mind. The 'Field' means the body and everything we experience.

gita-13-35.plain: Krishna says that people who see with wisdom the difference between the body (the Field) and the true Self that knows it (the Knower of the Field) become free from the hold of matter. Such people reach God, the Supreme.

gita-14-1.plain: Krishna says he will explain again the highest wisdom, the best of all knowledge. Wise people who learned it reached the highest goal.

gita-14-2.plain: Krishna says those who rely on this wisdom become like him. They are not born again when a new universe begins, and they are not shaken when it ends.

gita-14-3.plain: Krishna says that the great nature is like a mother's womb, and he places the seed of life into it. From this, all living beings are born.

gita-14-4.plain: Krishna says that whatever form a living being is born in, nature is its mother and he is its father. Every creature comes from him.

gita-14-5.plain: Krishna names the three qualities that come from nature: goodness, passion, and dullness. These three tie the soul that never dies to the body.

gita-14-6.plain: Krishna says goodness is pure, bright, and healthy. But even goodness ties a person down, by making them attached to happiness and to knowing things.

gita-14-7.plain: Krishna says passion creates strong wanting and craving. It ties the soul down by making it attached to always doing things.

gita-14-8.plain: Krishna says dullness comes from not knowing and fools everyone. It ties people down through carelessness, laziness, and too much sleep.

gita-14-9.plain: Krishna sums up: goodness ties us to happiness, passion ties us to action, and dullness hides wisdom and ties us to carelessness.
themes: why I keep acting this way

gita-14-10.plain: Krishna says the three qualities keep competing inside us. Sometimes goodness wins over the other two, sometimes passion wins, and sometimes dullness wins.
themes: why I feel different each day

gita-14-11.plain: Krishna says when clear understanding shines through all your senses, you can tell that goodness is growing in you.

gita-14-12.plain: Krishna says greed, busy energy, starting many projects, restlessness, and strong desire are signs that passion is growing.

gita-14-13.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that darkness of mind, feeling stuck, carelessness, and confusion are signs that dullness is growing.

gita-14-14.plain: Krishna says that if goodness is strongest when a person dies, they go to the pure worlds where the great wise ones live.

gita-14-15.plain: Krishna says that if passion is strongest at death, a person is reborn among busy, action-driven people. If dullness is strongest, they are reborn among beings without understanding.

gita-14-16.plain: Krishna says good action brings pure, peaceful results. Passion brings pain, and dullness brings ignorance.

gita-16-10.plain: Krishna says people with a demonic nature give in to desires that are never satisfied. They are full of vanity and arrogance, believe wrong ideas because they are confused, and act with selfish, unclean goals.

gita-16-11.plain: Krishna continues: such people are filled with endless worries that last until death. They think satisfying their desires is the most important thing and are sure that nothing else exists.

gita-16-12.plain: Tied up by hundreds of hopes and wants, and ruled by lust and anger, they try to pile up money by dishonest means so they can spend it on pleasures.

gita-16-13.plain: Krishna describes how such a person thinks: "I got this today, and I'll get that next. This money is already mine, and more will be mine later."

gita-16-14.plain: The proud person keeps thinking: "I beat this enemy, and I'll beat others too. I am the boss. I enjoy everything. I am perfect, strong and happy."

gita-16-15.plain: They also think: "I am rich and from a good family. Who is as great as me? I'll do religious rituals, give to charity, and enjoy myself." Krishna says this is how ignorance fools them.

gita-16-16.plain: Confused by many restless thoughts, trapped in a net of illusion, and hooked on pleasure, such people fall into a terrible hell.

gita-16-17.plain: Proud of themselves, stubborn, and drunk on their wealth, they perform religious rituals only in name, to show off, and not in the way scripture teaches.

gita-16-18.plain: Full of selfishness, love of power, rudeness, lust and anger, these hateful people hate God, who lives inside other people and inside themselves.

gita-16-19.plain: Krishna says that these hateful, cruel and wicked people are sent again and again to be born into families and lives with a demonic nature.

gita-16-20.plain: Born into demonic lives again and again, and staying confused each time, they never reach Krishna, Arjuna (called Kaunteya, son of Kunti). Instead they sink lower and lower.

gita-16-21.plain: Krishna says hell has three doors that destroy a person: lust, anger and greed. So everyone should give up these three.

gita-16-22.plain: A person who has escaped these three doors of darkness, Arjuna, does what is truly good for himself and reaches the highest goal.

gita-16-23.plain: Whoever ignores the teachings of scripture and just does whatever desire tells them will not find perfection, happiness or the highest goal.

gita-16-24.plain: So, Krishna tells Arjuna, let scripture be your guide for what to do and what not to do. Learn what it teaches, and then act in the world.

gita-17-1.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna: what about people who worship with real faith but don't follow the rules of scripture? Is their faith pure, passionate, or dark?

gita-17-2.plain: Krishna answers that the faith people are born with comes in three kinds: pure, passionate and dark. He says he will explain each one.

gita-17-3.plain: Krishna says each person's faith matches their own nature, Arjuna (called Bharata). A person is made of their faith: whatever they truly believe in, that is what they become.

gita-17-4.plain: Krishna says pure people worship the gods. Passionate people worship powerful spirits and giants. Dark people worship ghosts and spirits of nature.

gita-17-5.plain: Krishna begins describing people who do harsh, painful self-punishment that scripture does not ask for. They do it out of vanity and ego, driven by their desires and passions.

gita-18-18.plain: Krishna explains what pushes us to act: knowing something, the thing known, and the person who knows. Every action is also made of three parts: the tools used, the deed itself, and the doer.
themes: why we do what we do

gita-18-19.plain: Krishna says that knowledge, action and the doer each come in three kinds. This depends on the three qualities of nature, called gunas: goodness, passion and darkness. He asks Arjuna to listen as he explains them.

gita-18-20.plain: The purest kind of knowledge sees one eternal reality living in every being. It sees all beings as connected, even though they look separate.

gita-18-21.plain: Knowledge driven by passion sees all beings only as separate and different from each other. It misses the one reality that joins them.

gita-18-22.plain: The darkest kind of knowledge grabs onto one small thing as if it were everything. It is narrow, has no good reason behind it, and misses the truth.

gita-18-23.plain: A pure action is one that is your proper duty. You do it without craving the reward, without clinging, and without liking or hating anyone.

gita-18-24.plain: An action is driven by passion when it is done out of craving or to feed your ego. Doing it with great strain and struggle is also a sign of passion.

gita-18-25.plain: A dark action is done out of confusion. The person does not think about whether they can do it, what will happen, or how it might hurt others.

gita-18-26.plain: A pure doer is free from clinging and ego. They are steady and full of energy, and they stay the same whether they succeed or fail.
themes: staying calm in success and failure

gita-18-27.plain: A doer ruled by passion is eager for rewards, greedy and willing to harm. They are not clean in heart and are tossed around by joy and sorrow.

gita-18-28.plain: A dark doer is undisciplined, crude, stubborn, dishonest and spiteful. They are also lazy, gloomy and keep putting things off.

gita-18-29.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, whom he calls Dhananjaya (winner of wealth), that he will now explain the three kinds of reason (understanding) and of firmness (willpower).

gita-18-30.plain: Pure understanding knows when to act and when to hold back. It knows right from wrong duty, what to fear and what not to fear, and what traps us and what sets us free. Krishna calls Arjuna Partha, son of Pritha.
themes: when to act and when to wait

gita-18-31.plain: Understanding ruled by passion is confused about right and wrong. It cannot clearly tell what should be done and what should not.

gita-18-32.plain: Dark understanding is covered in ignorance. It thinks wrong is right and sees everything upside down.

gita-18-33.plain: Pure firmness is a steady willpower built through yoga practice. It keeps the mind, the breath and the senses under control.

gita-18-34.plain: Firmness ruled by passion holds tightly to duty, pleasure and wealth. It does this because it is attached and wants rewards.

gita-18-35.plain: Dark firmness is stubbornly holding on to too much sleep, fear, grief, gloom and pride, out of foolishness.
themes: unable to let go of fear

gita-18-36.plain: Krishna begins to describe three kinds of happiness. The first kind is a joy you grow into through practice, and it brings an end to suffering. He calls Arjuna 'bull of the Bharatas', meaning best of his family line.

gita-18-37.plain: Pure happiness feels like poison at first but becomes like sweet nectar in the end. It comes from clearly knowing your true Self.

gita-4-19.plain: Krishna says a true sage is someone who does his work without being driven by selfish wants. Wisdom burns away the hold that his actions could have on him, like fire burns wood.
themes: doing good for its own sake

gita-4-20.plain: Krishna says that a person who stops clinging to the results of his work stays content. He does not lean on anything outside himself for security. Even though he keeps working, it is as if he is not doing anything, because the work does not bind him.

gita-4-21.plain: Krishna says that a person who expects nothing, controls his mind, and has let go of greed does no wrong. Only his body does the work. His heart is not grabbing for gain.

gita-4-22.plain: Krishna says a person who is happy with whatever comes to him naturally, who is not thrown around by good and bad times, who is not jealous, and who stays calm whether he wins or loses, is not trapped by his actions.
themes: being content with what I have
staying calm in ups and downs

gita-4-23.plain: Krishna says that when a person's attachments are gone and his mind rests in wisdom, he does all his work as an offering. Then his actions no longer leave any binding effect on him.

gita-4-24.plain: Krishna describes a fire offering, the old Hindu ritual of pouring melted butter into a sacred fire. He says that everything in it is really the Eternal, meaning God or the ultimate reality: the offering, the butter, the fire, and the one who offers. A person who sees God in everything he does will reach God.

gita-4-25.plain: Krishna begins listing the different kinds of sacrifice, or spiritual offering. Some spiritual seekers make offerings to the gods, the "Shining Ones." Others offer themselves entirely into the Eternal.

gita-4-26.plain: Krishna says some people make an offering by holding back their senses, like hearing, through self-restraint. Others offer up the things they hear and see by using their senses in a disciplined, holy way.

gita-4-27.plain: Krishna says others use self-control to join with the Divine. In that union, which wisdom lights up like a fire, they offer up all the work of their senses and even their life energy.

gita-4-28.plain: Krishna lists more kinds of offering. Some give their wealth. Some practice hardship and self-denial. Some practice yoga. Some study holy books quietly and seek knowledge. All of them are focused and keep firm vows.

gita-4-29.plain: Krishna says some people make their offering through breath control. They carefully guide and pause the breath going in and out, and give their full attention to it.

gita-4-30.plain: Krishna says others eat in a controlled way and offer up their life energy that way. All these people understand what true sacrifice is, and through it they have cleansed themselves of wrongdoing.

gita-4-31.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, whom he calls "best of the Kurus" after his family line, that people who live on what is left from their offerings reach the eternal God. A person who never gives or sacrifices finds no real happiness even in this world, and still less in the next.

gita-4-32.plain: Krishna says there are many kinds of sacrifice, and all of them come from action. Knowing this truth will set Arjuna free.
themes: the role of action in spiritual life

gita-4-33.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, whom he calls Parantapa ("defeater of enemies") and Partha ("son of Pritha"), that offering wisdom is better than offering any material thing. All actions find their completion in wisdom.

gita-4-34.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to learn this wisdom by becoming a humble student, by asking questions, and by serving. Wise people who have seen the truth will teach him.

gita-4-35.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna, whom he calls Pandava ("son of Pandu"), that once he has this wisdom he will not be confused like this again. He will see every living being in his own true Self, and in Krishna.

gita-4-36.plain: Krishna says that even if Arjuna were the worst sinner of all, wisdom would carry him safely across all his sins, like a raft carries someone across a river.

gita-4-37.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that a blazing fire turns wood into ashes. In the same way, wisdom burns away the effects of all past actions.

gita-4-38.plain: Krishna says nothing in this world cleanses a person like wisdom does. A person who has mastered yoga, the practice of uniting with God, will find this wisdom inside himself when the time is right.

gita-2-34.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that if he runs away, people will talk about his shame forever. For someone who is deeply respected, losing honor is worse than dying.
themes: fear of what people will say
pressure to live up to expectations

gita-2-35.plain: Krishna warns that the great warriors who once admired Arjuna will think he ran away out of fear. They will stop respecting him.

gita-2-36.plain: Krishna says Arjuna's enemies will mock him and say cruel things about his strength. He asks what could hurt more than that.

gita-2-37.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called son of Kuntī, his mother) that he cannot lose by fighting. If he dies, he goes to heaven, and if he wins, he rules the earth, so he should stand up and fight with resolve.

gita-2-38.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, winning and losing as the same. If he fights with this calm, steady mind, he will do no wrong.
themes: staying calm whether I win or lose

gita-2-39.plain: Krishna says he has explained things through Sānkhya, the path of knowing the true self. Now he will teach Yoga, the path of right action, which will free Arjuna from the trap that actions create.
themes: learning a new way to see life

gita-2-40.plain: Krishna says no effort on this path is ever wasted, and nothing can go wrong by trying it. Even a little of this wisdom protects a person from great fear.

gita-2-41.plain: Krishna, calling Arjuna joy of the Kurus (his family line), says a firm mind is focused on one goal. A person who can't decide has endless scattered thoughts going in every direction.

gita-2-42.plain: Krishna says foolish people give fancy speeches and love only the surface words of the Vedas, the ancient holy texts. They claim there is nothing more to religion than that.

gita-2-43.plain: Krishna says these people are driven by selfish desire and only want heaven as a reward. They promote many rituals just to gain pleasure and power.

gita-2-44.plain: Krishna says people who cling to pleasure and power, and are carried away by such teachings, cannot develop a firm, focused mind for meditation.

gita-2-45.plain: Krishna says the Vedas deal with the three qualities of nature (the gunas: goodness, passion and dullness). He tells Arjuna to rise above them and above opposites like hot and cold or praise and blame, to stay pure and steady, not worry about owning things, and rest in his true Self.

gita-2-46.plain: Krishna says that for a wise person who knows the truth, the scriptures are like a small water tank in a place already flooded with water. They already have what the texts point to.

gita-2-47.plain: Krishna says you have a right only to do your work, never to control its results. Don't work just for the reward, but don't stop working either.

gita-2-48.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Dhananjaya, winner of wealth) to act while connected to God, letting go of attachment and staying the same in success or failure. This steady balance is what yoga means.
themes: staying balanced in success and failure

gita-2-49.plain: Krishna says action done for reward is far lower than action guided by wisdom. He tells Arjuna to rely on clear understanding, because people who work only for rewards are to be pitied.
themes: why I feel empty after success

gita-2-50.plain: Krishna says a person joined with true wisdom goes beyond both good and bad deeds and their effects. So hold on to yoga, because yoga means doing actions skillfully.

gita-2-51.plain: Krishna says wise people, joined with true understanding, give up the rewards of their actions. They become free from being born again and reach a state of peace and joy.

gita-2-52.plain: Krishna says when Arjuna's mind gets free of this confusion, he will no longer care about everything he has heard or will hear from teachings and opinions.

gita-2-53.plain: Krishna says Arjuna's mind is now confused by many scriptures. When it becomes still and steady in meditation, he will reach yoga.

gita-14-17.plain: Krishna says each of the three qualities of nature gives its own results. Harmony (goodness) brings wisdom. Motion (restless passion) brings greed. Inertia (dullness) brings carelessness, confusion and ignorance.

gita-14-18.plain: Krishna says people rooted in goodness rise upward to higher states. Restless, busy people stay in the middle. Dull, lazy people sink lower, wrapped in the worst qualities.
themes: does my character shape my future

gita-14-19.plain: Krishna says a wise person sees that the three qualities of nature are what really do all the acting. When that person also knows what lies beyond the qualities, they come to share Krishna's own nature.

gita-14-20.plain: Krishna says all bodies come from the three qualities. The soul living in the body can rise above them. Then it is free from birth, death, old age and sorrow, and it tastes a life that never ends.

gita-14-21.plain: Arjuna asks Krishna three questions. How can you recognize someone who has gone beyond the three qualities? How does that person behave? And how do they get beyond them?
themes: what does a spiritual person look like
how to rise above my nature

gita-14-22.plain: Krishna begins his answer to Arjuna, whom he calls Pandava (son of Pandu). Such a person does not hate clarity, busy energy or confusion when they show up. They also do not long for these when they are gone.

gita-14-23.plain: Krishna says this person sits calmly, like an onlooker, and is not shaken by the qualities. They tell themselves, "These are just the qualities moving around," and stay steady and apart.
themes: watching my emotions without being ruled by them

gita-14-24.plain: Krishna says this person stays the same in pleasure and pain and relies on their inner self. To them a lump of dirt, a stone and gold are worth the same. They treat pleasant and unpleasant people alike, and they stay steady whether blamed or praised.
themes: staying balanced in good and bad times

gita-14-25.plain: Krishna goes on: this person is the same in honor and in shame, and the same toward friends and enemies. They give up all self-driven projects. Such a person has gone beyond the three qualities.

gita-14-26.plain: Krishna says anyone who serves him with undivided, loving devotion also goes beyond the three qualities. Such a person becomes ready to be one with the Eternal.

gita-14-27.plain: Krishna says he is the home and foundation of the Eternal. He is also the source of everlasting life, of timeless goodness, and of happiness that never ends.

gita-15-1.plain: Krishna describes the world as an everlasting Asvattha, a sacred fig tree, growing upside down. Its roots are above and its branches below. Its leaves are the sacred hymns, and whoever understands this tree truly knows the Vedas (the holy scriptures).

gita-15-2.plain: Krishna says the tree's branches spread up and down, fed by the three qualities. The things we see, hear and taste are its buds. Its roots also reach down into the human world, where they tie people to their actions.
themes: why I feel stuck in life

gita-15-3.plain: Krishna says no one in this world can see the tree's true shape, its beginning, its end or where it is rooted. Still, this deep-rooted tree must be cut down with the strong axe of non-attachment, which means not clinging to things.

gita-15-4.plain: Krishna says that after cutting the tree, a person should seek the path beyond it, and whoever takes it never comes back to this world. They should seek shelter in the First Being, from whom all of creation first flowed.

gita-15-5.plain: Krishna says some people walk the path that never ends. They are free of pride and confusion and have beaten attachment. They stay focused on the true Self and have calmed their desires. Pleasure and pain no longer push them around.
themes: staying steady through ups and downs

gita-15-6.plain: Krishna says his highest home needs no sun, moon or fire to light it. Those who reach it never return to this world.

gita-15-7.plain: Krishna says each living soul is a small, eternal part of himself. Living in the world, it gathers around itself the five senses and the mind, and these are wrapped in matter.

gita-15-8.plain: Krishna says when the soul takes a body and when it leaves one, it carries the senses and mind along with it. It is like the wind carrying scents away from flowers.

gita-15-9.plain: Krishna says the soul lives in the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, nose and mind. Through them it experiences and enjoys the world.
themes: who is the one who feels

gita-3-2.plain: Arjuna tells Krishna that his mixed messages are confusing him. He asks Krishna to tell him clearly the one way that will lead to true happiness.

gita-3-3.plain: Krishna explains that there are two paths in life. One is the path of knowledge, followed by thinkers called Sankhyas. The other is the path of action, followed by people who serve through their work.
themes: different paths to the same goal
finding the right spiritual path for me

gita-3-4.plain: Krishna says you cannot become free just by refusing to act. Simply giving things up does not make a person perfect.
themes: does giving up things make me spiritual

gita-3-5.plain: Krishna says no one can stop acting, not even for a moment. Everyone is pushed to do things by the natural forces inside them.

gita-3-6.plain: Krishna says a person who holds his body still but keeps thinking about pleasures is fooling himself. Such a person is a fake.

gita-3-7.plain: Krishna says a person who controls his senses with his mind and does his work without clinging to results is truly worthy. This is the path of action.

gita-3-8.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to do his proper work. Acting is better than doing nothing, and without action you could not even keep your body alive.

gita-3-9.plain: Krishna says actions tie us down unless they are done as an offering. So Arjuna should act for that higher purpose, without being attached to what he gets out of it.

gita-3-10.plain: Krishna says that long ago the Creator made people along with sacrifice, or giving offerings. The Creator told them that through sacrifice they would grow and get what they wish for.

gita-3-11.plain: The Creator's words continue: people should care for the gods, the Shining Ones, through offerings, and the gods will care for people. By caring for each other, all will reach the highest good.

gita-3-12.plain: The gods, pleased by offerings, will give people the good things they want. But anyone who enjoys these gifts without giving anything back is like a thief.
themes: being thankful for what I have

gita-3-13.plain: Krishna says good people who eat what is left after making an offering are freed from wrongdoing. But selfish people who cook only for themselves are eating sin.

gita-3-14.plain: Krishna describes a cycle: living beings come from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.

gita-3-15.plain: Krishna says action comes from Brahma, the sacred word or Veda, and Brahma comes from the eternal God. So the eternal, everywhere-present God is always found in sacrifice.

gita-3-16.plain: Krishna says a person who does not take part in this turning cycle of giving, and lives only for pleasure, wastes his life.

gita-3-17.plain: Krishna says a person who finds full joy and contentment in the Self, the true inner spirit, has no duty left to do.

gita-3-18.plain: Such a person gains nothing by acting and loses nothing by not acting. He does not depend on anyone for anything.

gita-3-19.plain: So Krishna tells Arjuna to always do his duty without attachment. Working this way, a person reaches the Supreme, God.

gita-3-20.plain: Krishna points out that King Janaka and others reached perfection through action. Arjuna should also act, keeping the good of the world in mind.

gita-3-21.plain: Krishna says whatever a great person does, others copy. The example a leader sets is what people follow.

gita-11-27.plain: Arjuna sees the warriors of both armies rushing into the huge, terrifying mouths of the cosmic form. Some are caught between its teeth, their heads crushed.

gita-11-28.plain: Arjuna says the great kings and warriors rush into God's flaming mouths the way rivers rush into the ocean. They cannot stop themselves.

gita-11-29.plain: Arjuna compares the warriors to moths flying fast into a flame. Like the moths, they hurry into God's mouths and are destroyed.

gita-11-30.plain: Arjuna sees God's form swallowing people on every side with fiery tongues. Its blazing light fills space, and the whole universe seems to burn. Vishnu is a name for God.

gita-11-31.plain: Frightened, Arjuna bows and begs for mercy. He asks Krishna who he really is in this awful form, because he cannot understand what he is seeing.

gita-11-32.plain: Krishna answers that he is Time, which destroys the world. He says none of the warriors gathered here will escape death, except Arjuna and his side.

gita-11-33.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna to get up and fight. He says the enemies are already defeated by him, and Arjuna only needs to be the one who carries it out. 'Left-handed one' is a name for Arjuna, who can shoot arrows with either hand.
themes: being a tool of a bigger plan

gita-11-34.plain: Krishna names the great warriors on the other side, like Drona, Bhishma and Karna, and says he has already killed them. He tells Arjuna to fight without fear because he will win.

gita-11-35.plain: Sanjaya, the narrator telling the story to a blind king, says Arjuna trembled with fear. With palms joined, he bowed down low and spoke to Krishna again, stammering.

gita-11-36.plain: Arjuna says it is right that the world sings Krishna's praise with joy. The evil spirits (Rakshasas) run away in fear, and the perfected holy beings (Siddhas) bow down to him.
themes: the good rejoice, the evil flee

gita-11-37.plain: Arjuna asks how anyone could fail to bow to Krishna. He is the first cause of everything, greater even than Brahma the creator god, endless and undying, both what exists and what does not.

gita-11-38.plain: Arjuna praises Krishna as the first of the gods and the most ancient being. Everything that lives rests in him, he knows all and is what is known, and the whole universe is spread out in his form.

gita-11-39.plain: Arjuna says Krishna is all the gods: Vayu the wind, Yama the god of death, Agni the fire, the moon, and Varuna the god of waters. He is the father and grandfather of all, and Arjuna salutes him a thousand times.

gita-11-40.plain: Arjuna bows to Krishna in front, behind and on every side. Krishna's power has no limit, he holds everything, so he himself is everything.

gita-11-41.plain: Arjuna remembers that he used to treat Krishna as just a friend. He called him casual names like 'Krishna' or 'friend' out of love, without knowing how great he really was.

gita-11-42.plain: Arjuna asks forgiveness for any time he joked with Krishna or showed him disrespect. This includes while playing, resting, sitting, eating, alone or with friends.

gita-11-43.plain: Arjuna calls Krishna the father of everything that moves and stands still. He says Krishna deserves more respect than any teacher, and no one is equal to him or greater than him.

gita-11-44.plain: Arjuna bows down with his whole body and asks for Krishna's blessing. He asks Krishna to put up with him the way a father forgives a son, a friend forgives a friend, and a lover forgives the beloved.

gita-11-45.plain: Arjuna says he has seen what no one has seen before. He is glad, but his heart is shaking with fear, so he begs Krishna to show his other, gentler form again.

gita-11-46.plain: Arjuna asks to see Krishna as before, with a crown and a mace and discus in his hands. He wants Krishna to take his four-armed form again instead of this thousand-armed one.
themes: wanting a gentler face of God

gita-9-3.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Parantapa, "scorcher of foes") that people who have no faith in this knowledge do not reach God. Instead they keep coming back to this world, where everything dies, again and again.

gita-9-4.plain: Krishna says he fills the whole world in a form that cannot be seen. Every living being depends on him, but he does not depend on them.

gita-9-5.plain: Krishna adds a puzzle: in another sense, beings are not really held inside him either. He calls this his divine power. He holds up all beings and brings them into existence, yet he is not tied to them.
themes: how God relates to the world

gita-9-6.plain: Krishna gives an example. The wind blows everywhere, yet it always stays within the sky. In the same way, all beings live and move within him.
themes: God as the space we live in

gita-9-7.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Kaunteya, "son of Kunti") that at the end of each great age of the universe, all beings sink back into his nature. When a new age begins, he sends them out again.
themes: creation and destruction of the universe

gita-9-8.plain: Krishna says he uses his own nature to bring all beings into existence, over and over. The beings have no control over this, because the forces of nature carry them along.

gita-9-9.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Dhananjaya, "winner of wealth") that all this creating does not trap him. He stays above it all and is not attached to what he does.

gita-9-10.plain: Krishna says nature produces everything that moves and everything that stays still, while he watches over it. Because of this, the world keeps turning.

gita-9-11.plain: Krishna says foolish people look down on him when he appears in a human body. They do not understand that he is the great Lord of all beings.
themes: failing to see what is sacred

gita-9-12.plain: Krishna says such people have empty hopes, useless actions and no real understanding. Their minds are confused, and they take on a cruel, deceitful and demon-like nature.

gita-9-13.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (called Partha, "son of Pritha") that great souls, called Mahatmas, share in his divine nature. They know he is the everlasting source of all beings, and they worship him with a steady mind.

gita-9-14.plain: Krishna says these devoted people always praise him. They work hard, keep their promises, and bow down to him. Their worship is full of love and they stay steady in it.

gita-9-15.plain: Krishna says others worship him through knowledge, which they offer like a sacrifice. They see him as one God who is also present in many forms, everywhere.

gita-9-16.plain: Krishna says he is every part of the fire ritual. He is the act of worship, the offering to the ancestors, the healing herb, the sacred chant called a mantra, the butter poured in, the fire, and the offering itself.
themes: God in every part of worship

gita-9-17.plain: Krishna says he is the father, the mother, the supporter and the grandfather of the universe. He is the holy one to be known, the sacred sound Om, and the three ancient holy books called the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.

gita-9-18.plain: Krishna says he is the goal, the master, the lord, the witness, the home, the shelter and the friend. He is where all things begin and end, their foundation, their resting place, and the seed that never dies.
themes: where we come from and go

gita-9-19.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that he gives heat, and he holds back the rain or lets it fall. He is both immortality and death, both what exists and what does not.

gita-9-20.plain: Krishna says some people follow the three Vedas (holy books), drink the ritual drink called Soma, and offer sacrifices to ask for heaven. They go to the heaven of Indra, king of the gods, and enjoy heavenly pleasures there.

gita-9-21.plain: Krishna says that after these people enjoy heaven, their good merit runs out and they return to this world of death. Because they follow the rituals only to get what they want, they get only things that do not last.
themes: being good for the wrong reasons

gita-9-22.plain: Krishna says that people who worship him alone and think of nothing else, and who stay steady, are fully cared for. He gives them what they need and protects what they have.

gita-11-7.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna (here called Gudakesha, "one who has conquered sleep") to look at His body. The whole universe is there in one place, everything that moves and everything that stays still, plus anything else Arjuna wants to see.
themes: wanting to see the bigger picture

gita-11-8.plain: Krishna explains that Arjuna cannot see this form with his normal eyes. So Krishna gives him a "divine eye," a special power of sight, so he can see Krishna's full power.
themes: needing help to see the truth

gita-11-9.plain: Sanjaya, the narrator telling the story to the blind King Dhritarashtra, says that Krishna (also called Hari), the great master of yoga, now showed Arjuna (Partha) His highest form as Lord of all.
themes: the narrator reports to the king

gita-11-10.plain: Sanjaya describes the form. It had many mouths and eyes and showed many amazing sights. It wore many heavenly ornaments and held up many heavenly weapons.

gita-11-11.plain: The form wore heavenly necklaces and clothes and was covered in heavenly perfumed oils. It was full of wonders and had no limits, with faces looking in every direction.

gita-11-12.plain: Sanjaya says that if a thousand suns all blazed in the sky at once, their light might come close to the glory of that great being.

gita-11-13.plain: Arjuna (the Pandava, son of Pandu) saw the whole universe, with all its many different parts, gathered together in the body of Krishna, the God above all gods.

gita-11-14.plain: Arjuna (Dhananjaya) was filled with amazement, and his hair stood on end. He bowed his head to Krishna, pressed his palms together in respect, and began to speak.

gita-11-15.plain: Arjuna says he sees all the gods inside Krishna's form, along with every kind of living being. He sees Brahma, the creator god, sitting on his lotus seat, all the great sages (Rishis), and the divine serpents.

gita-11-16.plain: Arjuna says he sees Krishna everywhere, with countless mouths, eyes, arms and bodies. He cannot find where Krishna begins, where His middle is, or where He ends, because He has no limit.

gita-11-17.plain: Arjuna sees Krishna shining everywhere, holding a discus and a mace and wearing a crown. He blazes like fire and like the sun, so bright it is hard to look at, and too big to measure.

gita-11-18.plain: Arjuna praises Krishna as higher than anything the mind can think, never dying, the final resting place of everything, and present in all things. He calls Him the eternal protector of dharma (what is right) and the most ancient Person.

gita-11-19.plain: Arjuna sees that Krishna has no beginning, middle or end, and endless strength and arms. The sun and moon are His eyes. His face blazes like a sacred fire, and its heat burns the whole world.
themes: sun and moon as God's eyes

gita-11-20.plain: Arjuna says Krishna alone fills the earth, the sky, and all the space in between. When the three worlds see this terrifying form, they tremble with fear.

gita-11-21.plain: Arjuna sees groups of gods (Suras) entering into Krishna. Some fold their hands in fear and pray. Great sages and perfect beings (Siddhas) shout "Hail!" and sing loud songs of praise.

gita-11-22.plain: Arjuna lists many kinds of heavenly beings, such as Rudras, Vasus, Adityas, the Ashvins, Maruts, Gandharvas (heavenly musicians), Yakshas, Siddhas and even Asuras (demons). All of them are staring at Krishna in amazement.

gita-11-23.plain: Arjuna describes the huge form with many mouths, eyes, arms, legs and feet, and many frightening teeth. He says the whole world is terrified to see it, and so is he.

gita-11-24.plain: Arjuna says Krishna's form reaches the sky, glowing with many colors, with open mouths and huge shining eyes. Seeing this, Arjuna's heart is shaking, and he has lost his strength and his peace of mind. He calls Krishna Vishnu here.

gita-11-25.plain: Arjuna sees Krishna's teeth like the fires that destroy the world at the end of time. He is so lost he no longer knows which way is which and finds nowhere to feel safe. He begs Krishna for mercy, the shelter of all the worlds.

gita-11-26.plain: Arjuna begins describing what he sees. The sons of Dhritarashtra, all the kings fighting with them, Bhishma (Arjuna's great-uncle), Drona (his teacher), Karna (called the charioteer's son), and the best warriors on Arjuna's own side are all there.
